articleTitle: Performance Analyses of Boost and Interleaved Boost Converters used in Wireless EV Charging Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Hazardous emissions and greenhouse gases are produced by the burning and overuse of fossil fuels. Electric Vehicles (EVs) provide solutions for the conservation of conventional energy resources, pollution reduction for a safe environment, and zero-emission vehicles. EV charging can be done in two ways, either wired or wireless. Wired charging has barriers like high cost, limited consumer knowledge, limited driving range, etc., when compared to wireless charging. Moreover, wireless charging can provide automated charging, which is more safe and convenient. A wireless EV charging system employing an Interleaved Boost Converter (IBC) as the DC-AC converter is discussed along with its performance analysis. A performance comparison of conventional Boost Converter (BC) with IBC is done, which shows that the structure of the IBC reduces current ripples and losses, thus improving the overall system efficiency. The simulation results are presented to prove the effectiveness of IBC in the application of Electric Vehicle Wireless Charging Systems (EVWCSs).

articleTitle: Deep Learning Networks for Short Term Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Accurate forecasting of electrical loads is essential for a power system to operate reliably and economically. Load forecasting is necessary for optimal power generation. Accurate load forecasting results in efficient and economic utilization of electrical infrastructure. However, forecasting load is difficult because load changes regularly and is affected by a number of other factors like temperature, pressure, humidity, season, etc. The amount of data collected at various points of a smart grid is of high volume, variety, and veracity and have the characteristics of big data. Deep learning models are extensively used in short term load forecasting in order to manage the high volume of data. This paper focuses on application of deep learning model to forecast electrical load using Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN). The evaluation metrics R-Squared (R2), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) are used to compare these models. The Dayton Power and Light Company’s estimated energy consumption in Megawatts (MW) is the data set used to implement the deep learning models for short-term load forecasting. Adam optimization using TensorFlow framework is used in developing these models. The developed model is suitable for load forecasting in real time data also.

articleTitle: Computing Confidence Score for Neural Network Predictions from Latent Features
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: As machine learning (ML)-based systems become more commonplace in our daily lives, users should be able to trust the predictions made by the ML models. Inappropriate predictions may have disastrous effects depending on the context in which the ML model is applied. To decide whether to trust a classifier prediction or not, current methods use the probabilities associated with the model predictions or nearest neighbors of the predicted label. In this study, we present experiments that show how the distribution statistics of the latent space features can be used to accurately compute the output confidence of a model.Our method involves first mapping the latent space feature values from the penultimate layer of a model to a hypothesized prior distribution and then storing the parameters of the prior distributions for each node. The degree to which a trained model’s penultimate layer activations for a given sample match the previously stored distribution parameters for the predicted label determines the level of confidence associated with that prediction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of utilizing different statistical properties of the latent space activations in our confidence scoring algorithm and compare our algorithm’s results against Softmax probabilities based confidence scores on the CIFAR-10 and MNIST datasets. The results of the experiment show that the confidence score computation based on latent space activation statistics performs better than the Softmax based approach.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approach for Mixed type Wafer Defect Pattern Recognition by ResNet Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing process involves various steps: fabrication of Wafers, testing of wafers, assembly of each single die and package level final test. Out of which, testing of wafer for defect detection and classification is the most important step where defective dies are eliminated. This improves the efficiency of the overall manufacturing process. Semiconductor wafer defects can be basic defects or mixed defects containing two or more basic defects. Since these defects varied from wafer to wafer and are complex, the accuracy obtained from traditional deep learning model is poor. To address this problem, a semiconductor mixed defect pattern recognition based on Residual Network (ResNet) Architecture is attempted. Among the ResNet architectures, ResNet50 is selected for wafer defect pattern recognition which has a 50 layer structure. The model is evaluated based on data set with 15 mixed defect patterns which were generated from WM-811K wafer map data set. Training, testing and validation of the data set is done. The performance parameters are generated and compared the performance with four different architectures including Convolutional Neural Network(CNN). The training results indicate that the ResNet50 shows a better performance in terms of accuracy, precision, recall and F1 score.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-Based Control Strategy for Supercapacitor Assisted Battery Powered EV
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Hybrid Energy Storage Systems (HESS) are now being explored the most for performance improvement of EVs. HESS utilizes one or more energy storage systems, taking advantage of each. A hybrid topology of sources with complementary characteristics and an adaptive control strategy reduces battery-powered EVs’ frequent charging and discharging need. In this context, a battery and supercapacitor combination with a fuzzy control strategy is proposed in this paper. Supercapacitors can handle peak power in short time intervals. The battery can supply loads continuously for extended periods. A tiny battery with a lower peak power output is all needed when using a hybrid system. The high power density of SC results in performance improvement with reduced battery size. The results show that the proposed fuzzy controller operates satisfactorily with a supercapacitor-assisted battery-powered EV. The frequent charging and discharging of the battery can be reduced, thereby improving the life span of the battery.

articleTitle: Sentiment Prediction of IMDb Movie Reviews Using CNN-LSTM Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: This article describes sentiment classification of movie reviews given by the user using deep neural networks. Long short term memory (LSTM) and convolutional neural network (CNN) are two popular deep neural networks used for sentiment analysis. Sentiment analysis is carried out on internet movie dataset (IMDb) which consist of 50K movie reviews. CNN and LSTM architectures are used individually and later combination of CNN-LSTM architecture is used. Accuracy and loss metrics measures are plotted for each architecture where LSTM architecture outperforms compare to CNN and CNN-LSTM architecture. Accuracy of GRU, CNN, LSTM and CNN-LSTM architecures are 53% 85%, 87% and 85% respectively. Adam optimizer and binary cross entropy is used for loss function. CNN-LSTM model is very good for long term dependency and accuracy is also good. Combination of CNN-LSTM reduces a training time for larger dataset and CNN has a convolutional layer to extract information by a larger piece of text.

articleTitle: Analysis of Fiber Proportion in Lower Limb Muscles Using Smoothed Pseudo Wigner-Ville Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Muscle fiber composition is a key performance-determining factor in athletics. The proportion of slow-twitch fibers (STF) and fast-twitch fibers (FTF) may differ greatly in muscles due to factors such as genetics, training-induced changes, or underlying pathological conditions. This study investigates the fiber type proportion of lower limb muscles such as gastrocnemius lateralis (GL) and soleus (SOL) using surface electromyography. Isometric signals are recorded from both muscles during calf raise exercises. First and last one second epochs of the recorded signals correspond to non-fatigue (NF) and fatigue (F) zones respectively and are analyzed using smoothed pseudo Wigner-Ville distribution (SPWVD). Two features namely spectral entropy (SE) and peak frequency (PF) are extracted from both zones. During fatigue, SE shows a decline of 4.87% in GL and an increase of 3.7% in SOL. Similarly, a 65.3% decrease in PF in GL and 41% increase in SOL is observed. The reduction of SE and PF in GL may be due to the fatigue of FTF whereas the increment of these features in SOL might be due to the greater proportion of STF. The decrease of SE in GL reflects the reduction of complexity with fatigue. Hence, the extracted features are found effective in identifying the fiber type proportion of these muscles. The proposed approach can be used for fiber-type assessment in sports science and biomedicine.

articleTitle: Implementing a land registration system using non-fungible tokens to represent land in the system and side-chain for data storage
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Blockchain Technology has been increasing in popularity in recent times due to its decentralized nature, immutability, transparency, high security and transparency. Several private and public organisations have been using it to develop new and innovative projects like cryptocurrency, NFTs, Metaverse, etc., and also to upgrade and improve old technologies like supply chains in agriculture and government voting systems. Land Registration is one such sector that can be upgraded using blockchain because in the current system there are a lot of middlemen involved and data is centralized and not secure, these things make the current system vulnerable to frauds and corruption. In this paper we have proposed a new implementation for the existing land registration system in the country that uses Non-Fungible tokens in the blockchain to represent a property and a sidechain like IPFS for storing its data in a decentralized manner. With our implementation we can overcome the flaws in the old system and make land registration secure, transparent and trustless. Here by "trustless" we mean that users do not have to trust any centralized authority or intermediary to verify transactions or maintain the integrity of the system. Instead, trust is placed in the system’s consensus mechanism and cryptographic protocols.

articleTitle: Detection of typical Pathologies and Differential Treatments in Dental Panoramic X-Rays based on Deep Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is gaining traction in medical imaging. There are a plethora of potential applications, covering every stage of the medical imaging life cycle from image creation to diagnosis to outcome prognosis. The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning is having a rising influence in the field of dentistry and is improving the growth of digital tools and technology, with a wide range of applications in cosmetic dental treatments and treatment planning. Deep learning has been able to match and improve human performance in fields such as image processing for extremely complex tasks such as object detection models with classification and prediction capabilities, as well as the identification of numerous dental diseases and their differential treatments. The lack of sufficiently large, curated, and representative training data with expert labeling (eg, annotations) is one of the main barriers to the development and clinical application of AI algorithms. This pilot study used a dataset of 664 dental panoramic X-ray images to build a model that can detect dental diseases and the differential treatments present on a full dental X-ray. After being manually labeled for 9 different classes, these images were used for training. The deep neural network used in this study is You Only Look Once (YOLO) version 6, a one-step search method primarily used for real-time object detection. Three classes of dental diseases and six classes of differential treatments were identified with the aid of bounding boxes. Results show that this strategy was able to attain a mean average precision (mAP) of 70.76% by training with this smaller number of images, which shows tremendous potential for dentists and radiologists.

articleTitle: Design of Hexapod Robot with Adaptive Gait Transition on Rough Terrain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Legged robots has an advantage over wheeled robots when it comes to moving through rough terrain, they also consume less energy than a UAV with identical payload and can operate over a comparatively extended period of time. Hexapod robots are an important classification of legged robots because of their high load carrying capacity and improved stability. Multiple walking gaits or algorithms can be developed for hexapod robots. In this project a hexapod robot is to be designed and developed with each leg having 3 degrees of freedom and must posses the ability to adapt its walking gait ie it should vary its walking speed and change its walking gait in accordance with the roughness of the terrain. The various applications of this project include search and rescue, surveillance, terrain mapping etc.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Wireless System for drone to drone opportunity charging in a multi agent system
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: With the increasing need for packet deliveries, inspections, surveillance, crop spraying etc, the world is moving towards an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) or drone ecosystem which will require more workforce for manual plugin charging. Wireless Power Transfer is an inspiring technology for the autonomous charging of drones to reduce human interventions. However, the usage of drones is less widespread thanks to their short flight time of 30-40 minutes. In this paper drone to drone opportunity charging is studied to increase its flight time which is specifically relevant in multi-agent systems. A wireless bidirectional dual active bridge (DAB) converter is designed and simulated in MATLAB/SIMULINK.

articleTitle: Design of a Versatile Soft Pneumatic Gripper
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Conventional robotic grippers are rigid mechanisms that use suction for grasping objects and are often not used in areas like the food/agriculture industries due to the highly varying sizes, shapes, and weights of the objects which should be handled by them. Since they are designed for specific use cases which are often well-known in advance they are not designed to handle requirements like fragility, deformity, etc. Soft robotic grippers are a solution to this. With the increase in human-robot interactions and increased usage of co-bots, the need for soft robotic grippers is also growing. but often they too are designed for specific needs only. This paper discusses the design of a soft pneumatic gripper with a variable fixture, which can change the grasping workspace area accordingly to make the gripper more versatile. This will enable the gripper to be used in various situations where a traditional gripper requires manual/automated end-effector swap. The finite element analysis of the soft pneumatic actuator and the structure is performed and the parts are fabricated. The bending action of the soft pneumatic actuator is evaluated.

articleTitle: Optimization Strategies for Low-Latency 5G NR LDPC Decoding on General Purpose Processor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: In recent years, with the progression of the computational abilities of General-Purpose Processors (GPPs), there has been a heightened interest in the implementation of software Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) decoders. This investigation provides a comprehensive analysis of the most effective strategies for optimizing the decoding latency of 5G LDPC on GPPs. Our proposed optimization mechanisms consist of the implementation of Advanced Vector Extensions 512 (AVX-512) instructions in computationally intensive routines and the application of code transformation techniques, specifically optimization through unrolling to tackle the primary computational challenges and minimize the overall latency of the decoder. To assess the efficiency of our proposed techniques, thorough simulations were carried out to determine the decoding time. Our findings indicate that the implementation of the aforementioned optimization techniques on computational routines causing time bottlenecks can lead to a significant reduction of at least 30% in computational delay, even under unfavorable conditions. This discovery demonstrates the feasibility of developing a low-latency software 5G NR LDPC decoder on an x86 architecture.

articleTitle: Comparison Analysis of Various Optimization Algorithms for Classification of Radar Returns from the Ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Machine learning is developing swiftly as an everexpanding field. The development of the same is occurring rapidly and has made many theoretical breakthroughs in recent times. Due to its importance as a part of machine learning, intelligent optimization algorithms are expected to become increasingly. The exponential growth of data volume and the increase in model complexity present increasing challenges for machine learning optimization strategies. Numerous initiatives have been launched to improve machine learning optimization approaches or address optimization-related problems. Future optimization and machine-learning research can be guided by a detailed evaluation and analysis of optimization strategies from a machine-learning perspective. Machine learning uses a variety of optimization strategies, which makes it easier to compare and analyze how well they function in various situations. In this study, we analyze and contrast seven well-known bio-inspired data engineering techniques and their effectiveness. We apply these techniques to the Radar Returns from the Ionosphere data-set and assess the results with a range of assessment metrics.

articleTitle: Altitude and Attitude Control of X-Configuration Quadrotor Design
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The quadrotor type of UAV would presumably be the most prevalent form of UAV vehicle commercially available for civilian and defence purposes as it does not require intricate remote-controlling abilities to operate. However, this reputation hasn’t been matched by many studies in the field of dynamic modelling, architecture, and analysis of quadrotors. This research utilises MATLAB and Simulink tools to establish a mathematical modelling strategy for an X-configuration quadrotor design. The primary objective is to devise an appropriate mathematical model for quadrotors, assess the system’s performance, and keep the quadrotor stable under various flight circumstances. Along with the model, four basic PID-based automatic control strategies were also designed, i.e., for pitch, roll, yaw, and altitude hold systems. The model and the proposed control system were then evaluated in a sequence of simulation tests, which produced satisfactory results in simulating a quadrotor system. The developed model has good potential as a base for quadrotor analysis and control design.

articleTitle: A Space Vector PWM Signal Generation for Five Level Five Phase Inverter Drives
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: A space vector PWM (SVPWM) method for a five phase five level inverter is proposed. Two three level inverters are fed from opposite ends of an open end winding induction motor to create five level inversion. The proposed scheme is based on adding an offset voltage to the sampled reference voltage to achieve multilevel operation. The use of carrier region to identify the reference location will simplify the implementation of the algorithm. The eligible vectors, regions and switching sequence of the five vectors that define the accessible region can be directly determined from the modulation index value. This makes it easier to implement the optimal five vectors, and it is extendable to any multiphase multilevel inverter (odd number of levels) by simply changing the carrier region. The proposed algorithm was simulated in MATLAB/SIMULINK, and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of a MEMS Gyroscope Using Filtering and Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Gyroscopes are sensors used to measure angular rate and find wide application in the aerospace industry. MEMS Gyroscopes have various advantages of lesser cost, mass, size, power but with a corresponding decrease in performance parameters. Noise is a limiting factor in MEMS sensors leading to poor Drift Stability, higher Angular and Rate random walks which will in turn affect the output of the sensors. Also, the thermal effect on MEMS sensors is well-documented as a limitation to their wide deployment as sensors in uncontrolled environments. A novel digital filtering method is introduced and carried out on the data, and by means of trimming the filter parameters, processed data of different bandwidth was obtained. Statistical measurements were done on the processed data and 90 percent improvement was obtained in the short-term stability, which highlights the efficiency of the filtering process. A temperature control algorithm is introduced for operation of sensor at stable temperature. Also, a Neural Network based learning approach is used to train the data with respect to temperature as the major parameter. When it was tested with original sensor data, a 100percent improvement in short term stability was obtained.

articleTitle: FOC Based Control of a SynRM for Space Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Synchronous reluctance motors (SynRMs) are getting precedence now a days in industries compared to its contenders like induction motors because of its higher efficiency and cold rotor construction. SynRM suffers from torque ripples and power factor issues. Non linear behavior in torque production averts its use in high efficient control and drive schemes. In this work, a control scheme which reduces the torque ripple and improves the dynamic response of a SynRM is proposed. An additional torque control loop is incorporated to the standard structure of field oriented control (FOC). The proposed system is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink and the results illustrate that there is significant reduction in torque ripple with the proposed method.

articleTitle: Hybrid Multilevel Inverter Control for Harmonic Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Multilevel inverters are superior to conventional two level inverters in high and medium power industrial applications. A hybrid multilevel inverter control is proposed to mitigate the harmonic distortions in the output phase voltage waveforms of induction motor drives. An open-ended induction motor fed with a neutral point clamped three level main inverter on one side and a two level inverter with a floating capacitor on the other side is proposed. The two level inverter is switched to act as a series active filter with null active power supply to the motor, while the three level inverter is pulsed using space vector modulation technique. Thus, the two level inverter will cancel out the voltage distortions in the motor phase voltages. With this configuration, the motor phase voltage harmonic distortions are within the IEEE 519 standards, thereby improving the drive efficiency and motor life-span. The proposed system is simulated and collated with three level neutral point clamped inverter and dual inverter fed open-ended induction motor drive and found to have better harmonic performance.

articleTitle: Artificial Magnetic Conductor Based Multi Slotted Patch Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The field of wireless communication for Internet of Things (IoT) medical applications necessitates low-profile antenna solutions. In this study, an Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) technology-based patch antenna was developed, featuring circular-shaped patches with circular slots and a dual-band 4 × 4 array of AMC surface. In addition, defected ground structures were incorporated to enhance radiation characteristics in the 1.85 GHz, 2.45 GHz, and 5.3 GHz bands. The patch antenna was compact, measuring 0.95λ<inf>0</inf> × 1.13λ<inf>0</inf> × 0.028λ<inf>0</inf>. A dual-band symmetrical AMC unit cell measuring 22 × 22 × 1.6 mm<sup>3</sup> was subsequently designed, with a 15mm gap separating the patch antenna from the AMC surface. The antenna was supported by a 4 × 4 AMC array measuring 1.55λ<inf>0</inf> × 1.55λ<inf>0</inf> × 0.32λ<inf>0</inf> and resonating at a frequency of 5.3 GHz. Simulations indicated reflection coefficient values below -10 dB in 1.7–2.8 GHz and 5.2–5.4 GHz bands, with an impedance bandwidth of 48.8% and 3.77%, respectively, for the AMC integrated antenna. The proposed AMC surface complied with the WHO’s Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) criteria, with SAR values of 0.28 W/kg and 0.48 W/kg at 2.45 GHz and 5.3 GHz, respectively, and a maximum gain of 7.5dBi. The antenna and AMC structure design were well-suited for IoT-based healthcare systems, particularly ISM and WLAN applications.

articleTitle: Synchronous Reference Frame Theory Based Shunt Active Filter For Harmonic and Unbalance Compensation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Today’s power requirements are vastly different from those of the past, due to the growing utilization of nonlinear loads. Most of the power electronic loads used in the system are mainly nonlinear, which can lead to system inefficiencies and poor power factor. These kinds of loads introduce a lot of harmonics into the power system, increasing energy losses and having an impact on nearby loads and sources. Active filters are employed to compensate for harmonic distortion, reactive power, and unbalance generated by nonlinear loads. This paper proposes a shunt active power filter for harmonic and unbalance compensation in power system connected with a nonlinear and unbalanced load. The control scheme is based on synchronous reference frame theory, to extract the reference current. The model is validated using simulation studies in MATLAB/SIMULINK. The proposed shunt active power filter has the potential to significantly reduce harmonics, unbalance, and also improves the system power factor.

articleTitle: Grid Integrated Solar Photovoltaic Converter Control for Power Quality Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: In recent years, distributed generation systems derived from renewable sources like solar photovoltaic systems, fuel cells, wind farms etc. are picking upstream because of the growing demand for green energy. Battery energy storage systems are used for storing the energy generated form these renewable sources and are integrated using power converters to the utility grid system. A control strategy for the grid integrated photovoltaic converter is presented in this paper to mitigate the power quality issues owing to the connected non-linear loads. The grid integrated inverter is equipped with additional functionalities such as mitigation of harmonic distortions, reactive burden control and system power factor improvement along with power flow control. The fundamental active component of balanced load current is extracted to derive the reference compensating signal for the inverter. Thus, the grid-tied inverter will function like a shunt connected active filter at the point of common coupling to enhance the power quality of the utility grid. The analysis of the proposed scheme for photovoltaic fed inverter operation with simulation study reveals that the system satisfies the power quality standards.

articleTitle: Detecting Alzheimer’s Disease using Multi-Modal Data: An Approach Combining Transfer Learning and Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is a serious and irreversible brain condition that leads to the degeneration of cognitive and memory functions. The medical field has found deep-learning models to be effective in addressing this neuro-degenerative disorder causing brain damage and mental deterioration. Deep-learning methods are found to be effective in tasks such as identifying patterns in medical images and assisting with diagnostic decisions. Transfer learning, which utilizes a pre-trained model for a new task, can be particularly beneficial when data is limited. Using transfer learning, researchers have been able to accurately detect AD. In this work, a fusion of deep-transfer learning models and custom models are used to process clinical data and MRI images of AD patients as well as normal cohorts. Features from input MRI axial slices are extracted using EfficientNet-B3 and ResNet-152, and a two-layer fully connected network are employed to obtain features from clinical data, resulting in an accuracy of 99.65% in AD and NC classification through a fivefold cross-validation.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Control of an Autonomous Vehicle using Model Predictive Control and PID Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Over the years, there has been a substantial increase in the number of vehicular traffic, which has led to vital problems like car crashes and congestion. More than 90 percent of collisions are the result of human error. Technology that allows for autonomous driving has the potential to enhance traffic efficiency and safety. Based on knowledge about the nearby traffic, an autonomous vehicle can create a trajectory and follow it using control algorithms. A significant technology in the study and implementation of autonomous vehicles is trajectory tracking control. Paths are a series of instructions that provide directional directives to get to a specific location, whereas a trajectory includes the schedule of velocity and higher order words, such as acceleration in terms of the body’s longitudinal and lateral motion, that are necessary to reach there. In this study, PID controllers and model predictive controllers (MPC) are used to govern the trajectory of an autonomous vehicle. The performance of the autonomous vehicle using both the controllers are then compared. The work is validated using simulations on MATLAB simulink.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Voltage Level Shifter with Configurable Voltage Range
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Advancements in semiconductor device technology is reducing the size of Integrated Circuits. The operating voltages also are reducing in a similar fashion. Here comes the need for using devices operating at different voltages. The communication between devices working at different voltage levels may go erroneous when direct interface is attempted between them. This happens due to the noise margin issues. A voltage level shifter is a device, which is used to interface between two devices operating at different voltages so that the communication between them is proper. A bidirectional voltage level shifter with configurable voltage range is designed. The proposed voltage level shifter is having easily scalable number of channels configured as blocks which can be controlled independently. Each block consisting of a number of channels for which the direction of voltage level shifting is switchable and the voltages configurable within a wide range. SPICE simulations carried out shows the circuit properly operating in 1.2V to 1.8V range.

articleTitle: AMS circuit modeling by Bayesian Model Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The high data usage, scaling technology, and high simulation costs that are encountered when modeling the circuit performance of analog and mixed-signal circuits are some of the challenges that these models confront. A novel strategy is put forth to deal with this conflict, and a new modeling algorithm called Bayesian Model Fusion is used (BMF). The key element of BMF is the use of previously borrowed data to model the circuit’s performance at a later stage. The Bayesian Inference principle is used to extract data from the early stage. It makes use of Bayes theorem-based pre-silicon validation and post-silicon tuning methodologies to make this possible.

articleTitle: Demand forecasting in smart homes using deep learning techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: As energy usage grows quickly, smart energy management solutions have gained in popularity. Smart meters are used to track daily energy consumption in realtime. Demand forecasting is very important in smart homes where the smart meter data is used to forecast the load of a particular household and it can be even used for a neighbourhood. Prediction of electrical loads can be done using different deep learning techniques and can be used for demand management. Deep learning techniques proposed in this work include LSTM, Bi-LSTM and GRU. The proposed model for the prediction of energy consumption consists of data preprocessing, model generation and validation. The main benefit of this demand forecasting is to decrease energy wastage and improve energy consumption effectiveness.

articleTitle: Estimation of Ad Hoc Communication Channel using Stochastic Filters
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Ad hoc networks differ from conventional cellular networks in terms of their flexible infrastructure. In a cellular network, either the transmitter or the receiver is stationary, whereas in ad hoc networks, there is direct communication between mobile transmitters and receivers via a wireless medium. The temporal variations occurring in the propagation environment of ad hoc networks are mainly due to the nodes moving at varying speeds and the instantaneous appearance or disappearance of existing paths between transmitters and receivers. The time-varying statistics of wireless channels are known to be captured effectively by the dynamic models based on stochastic differential equations (SDEs). This paper proposes a scheme for the estimation/ identification of an ad hoc channel dynamically modelled via SDEs using the Ensemble square root filter (EnSRF). The channel states and parameters are estimated from the dynamic models arrived at by the factorization of the fundamental channel characteristic called Doppler power spectral density (DPSD), followed by a stochastic realization. The stochastic realization brings the channel model to a state space form viable for the chosen stochastic filtering frameworks. The constant parameters of the channel model, so derived, are realized using random walks and are augmented to the state space to enable a joint state and parameter estimation. A dynamic SDE-based channel model belonging to an urban environment with a predominant fading is adopted in numerical illustrations. Simulation results indicate remarkably superior accuracy and filter convergence of EnSRF estimates.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization based Current Control and Torque Control for 8/6 Switched Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The high torque ripples developed in the switched reluctance motor (SRM) limit its usage for high-performance applications. The methods designed to lower the torque ripple affects the efficiency of drive system. This paper introduces a comprehensive analysis of particle swarm optimization (PSO) based tuning of the hysteresis current controller and direct instantaneous torque controller for a 4-phase 8/6 SRM. The controller parameters and commutation angles are optimized for reduced torque ripple, improved efficiency, and better steady-state performance. Simulations are run in the MATLAB/SIMULINK environment and the results support the efficacy of the suggested method.

articleTitle: An Area Optimized Floating-Point Coprocessor for RISC-V Processor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we outline the design and development of an area optimized Floating-Point Unit (FPU) in accordance with the IEEE 754-2008 standard. This FPU acts as a coprocessor for RISC-V ISA based VEGA processor. The FPU supports both in-order and out-of-order execution of 58 RISC-V floating-point instructions with partial pipelining.

articleTitle: Domain Adaptation for Semantic Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Models that have the learning ability to overcome the domain shift between synthetic images and real-world images provide satisfactory results in real-world implementation even if they are trained on synthetic images. This eliminates the need for collection and annotation of real-world data which is not just time-consuming and expensive, but oftentimes impractical. With the advent of Transformers, research focus in this area is directed towards improving model capability rather than domain adaptability. The paper proposes an improved adversarial domain adapted segmentation network that uses feature distillation loss. The model uses CNN architecture DeepLabv2 as the backbone and a rare class sampler is also used for the source domain. An additional ImageNet feature distance loss is used for faster convergence and improved performance. The model trained on synthetic images is evaluated using real traffic images from Cityscapes dataset and also Kerala traffic images from Google to determine model adaptability.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of CZTSSe-Based Solar Cell With ZnS as Novel Buffer Layer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Currently, CZTSSe-based thin-film solar cells are the most efficient ones on the market. In most of the solar cells, Cadmium Sulphide (CdS) material is used as a buffer layer.Since it have a toxic nature it is replaced with some other material.Wide band gap, non-toxic zinc sulphide (ZnS) has the potential to take the place of cadmium sulphide (CdS) as the buffer layer in CZTSSe-based solar cells.Using the simulator Scaps, we perform a simulation study of a CZTSSe-based solar cell with ZnS as a buffer layer.There is an increase in efficiency by replacing CdS with ZnS.The efficiency of CZTSSe based solar cell with CdS as a buffer layer is 11.90%. However ,the simulated efficiency of CZTSSe based solar cell with ZnS as the buffer layer is 14.01%.The impacts of layer parameters on the photovoltaic parameters of the ZnS/CZTSSe solar cell are optimized, including the thickness, donor and acceptor densities of the CZTSSe absorber and ZnS buffer layers enhancing the ZnS/CZTSSe solar cell’s performance.To discover the suitable thickness for the solar cell, the thickness of the CZTSSe as absorber layer and the ZnS as buffer layer are both varied.Solar cell with the proposed model results ,the formation of solar cell having higher conversion rate and low priced.

articleTitle: PacketChain: A Blockchain-inspired Method for Enhanced Security of Packet Communication of Highly Constrained IoT Wearable Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) is one of the emerging technologies that play a central role in developing Industry 4.0. IoT has significant potential to revolutionize various industries by integrating connected devices, allowing for improved efficiency and automation. However, the widespread adoption of wearable IoT devices has also increased security concerns, particularly regarding personal data and privacy. Ensuring security for highly resource-constrained IoT devices, such as wearable devices, is paramount for our safety. Due to the device-level constraints and highly limited resources of IoT devices, traditional cyber privacy and security solutions are unsuitable for many IoT applications and systems. The concept of Blockchain, which forms the foundation of distributed ledger and cryptocurrency, is a potential candidate for enhancing the communication security of IoT. We propose PacketChain, a Blockchain-inspired method for ensuring packet transmission security for highly constrained wearable IoT devices. The proposed PacketChain method provides an additional security mechanism complementing the current cryptographic approaches and solutions used by IoT devices. PacketChain provides an application layer solution where one packet’s hash value is included in the subsequent packet, thereby, creating a chain of packets. Using PacketChain, many attacks can be quickly detected and avoided. PacketChain is designed at low complexity and overhead, and highly resource- constrained wearable IoT devices can use it. We implement the PacketChain solution and experimentally found its suitability in IoT applications. PacketChain can avoid or reduce the impact of several cyber attacks, such as packet drop, packet fake, TCP header hijack, and packet replay attacks which are major types of man-in-the-middle attacks.

articleTitle: A Novel General Purpose Processing ASIC for Inertial Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: High-performance inertial sensors are widely used for autonomous navigation, guidance and control applications. This requires its electronics to be co-located to the sensor with the best C-SWaP(Cost, Size, Weight, and Power) configuration. Analog circuit-based designs were implemented earlier for such requirements. However, such implementations require manual adjustment of circuit parameters based on sensors and are complex. The digital implementation provides reconfigurability and high performance. However, different kinds of sensors require different processing logic. The typical sensor processing requirements are accomplished by data converters and digital processing logic. The digital processing logic requirement may vary with respect to different kinds of sensors. However, all these requirements can be met by implementing different combinations of the following modules, like IIR, FIR, PID controller and oscillators. Hence, a novel CISC processor with the support of all these logic modules is implemented. The logic modules are fully configured by microcode-based programs and execute in different sequential orders based on sensor requirements. The above implementation has been completely implemented in FPGA and successfully interfaced with various MEMS Gyros and Accelerometers. Further ASIC realization was also carried out on the SCL-180nm Technology node with an area of 2 mm × 2 mm and a CQFP-64 pin package.

articleTitle: Low frequency radar for improving radar cross section
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Stealth or lower visibility is an inevitable feature of future-generation aircraft. A stealth aircraft is coated with a special type of material called radar absorbing material (RAM), which makes the aircraft invisible to radar. Stealth technology is a great threat to the Radar surveillance system. Anti-stealth radar can be built using low-frequency signals that are efficient in detecting stealth aircraft. The variation of radar cross section (RCS) under low frequency radar system is studied here also designed an antenna for low frequency radar.

articleTitle: A Configurable, Multi-Channel, Direct Wideband RF Sampling SWaP-C Optimized Transceiver and Processing Module for EW Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The rapid change nature of threats and rising demand for SWaP-C solution compels avoiding noisy RF down-converters and moving towards a digital processing directly at RF, enhancing system flexibility and sensitivity. Direct wide band sampling eliminates JESD204B reducing latency and eases configuration compared to prior art.In this paper, an approach to provide a configurable, multi-channel, direct wideband RF sampling transceiver and processing unit for EW System with SWaP-C optimization to latest technology has been explored.

articleTitle: Estimation of continuous blood pressure from pressure pulse wave morphology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Hypertension is the significant cause of death and many disabilities. Blood pressure is an index for knowing the cardiovascular status. More accurate continuous blood pressure can be obtained by arterial cannulation technique. Drawback with this method is that it causes potential risk to patient due to its invasive nature. Currently existing cuff based and oscillometric methods provide only short time data and it cannot be used for continuous monitoring. The purpose of this study is to estimate the continuous blood pressure using the pressure pulse wave morphology. Radial artery pressure pulse wave is used for the estimation. Initial blood pressure obtained with the help of regression model is added with the pressure difference between the systolic and diastolic feature points to evaluate the continuous blood pressure. About eleven informative features were extracted from pressure pulse wave and two regression models were constructed for comparing the performance. From mean absolute error calculated for the two models, multivariable linear regression model showed better accuracy than deep learning regression model. Initial blood pressure measured by multi-variable linear regression model is added with pressure difference to estimation continuous systolic and diastolic blood pressure. The results showed the reliability of pressure pulse wave morphology for non invasive blood pressure estimation.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Sliding Free-standing Mode Triboelectric Nanogenerator (TENG) Based Sensors for IoT applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a ground-breaking technology that aims to connect anything from anywhere at any time. The IoT has been influencing our lifestyle in many ways from home appliances that we can control with our smartphones to self-driving smart cars finding best travel routes based on traffic data. With the rapid development of IoT and sensor technologies, there is a huge demand for sensors with inbuilt power sources and human-machine interfaces (HMIs). Triboelectric Nanogenerator also known as TENG, is a novel device that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by utilizing the energy wasted in our ambient environment thus eliminating the need for costly power supplies required to power the sensors. TENG can also act as a human-machine interface for supervising human-machine interactions. This paper presents the performance comparison of simple & low-cost TENG-based sensors for IoT applications. The paper evaluates the effectiveness of the freestanding mode TENG-based sensor towards the Internet of Things (IoT) applications. Experiments are conducted to show that TENG-based sensors are capable of generating signals for wireless control applications.

articleTitle: Self-supported Dynamic Voltage Restorer for Power Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Voltage power quality issues are the most severe and common power quality issues in an electrical power distribution network. Sophisticated equipment for industrial and domestic consumers is sensitive to voltage quality issues and hence to be mitigated effectively. Dynamic voltage restorer (DVR) provides a versatile and cost-effective solution for compensating voltage-related power quality issues. This paper presents the design and simulation of a 50kVA three-phase self-supported DVR. Each phase sag is compensated individually by using three single-phase inverters. The DC voltage for the single-phase inverters is maintained by a three-phase front-end converter. Line frequency transformer is avoided for connecting the three-phase active front-end converter to reduce the size of DVR. The topology, configuration, and control strategy are examined with simulation in PSIM.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of a High Speed Efficient Single Precision Floating Point ALU
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Modern-day computing processors require efficient floating point processing units that operate with high speed and low power consumption. Floating point computation operations are used in a wide variety of applications across different fields such as Engineering, AI, ML and DSP due to their inconceivable dynamic range and enhanced accuracy. These operations need to be performed quickly, with low power consumption and minimal hardware usage. In this paper, we present an efficient single precision floating point arithmetic logic unit with optimized architectures for addition and subtraction using carry look-ahead adder, multiplication using a modified booth encoder and division using the Goldschmidt algorithm. Our proposed architecture is designed using Verilog HDL and implemented on the Spartan 7 FPGA. The implemented design is compared with an existing ALU architecture and we demonstrate that the proposed ALU is 36% faster and more efficient in terms of power and area.

articleTitle: Simulation and Validation of a Precise 2RC Model of Lithium-Ion cell Incorporating Wire-bond Losses
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Li-ion cell is a popular electrochemistry for energy storage devices in electric vehicles and portable electronics. This is mainly due to their relatively high energy-density and power-density compared to other types of battery chemistry. In a battery pack, several li-ion cells are interconnected in a series-parallel fashion to meet the current and voltage demands of the load. Interconnecting wires or wire-bonds add parasitic resistance to the current path, contributing to power loss. Therefore, it is essential to include wire-bond losses in the battery model to get an accurate prediction of battery performance. In this paper, the authors have developed a 2RC model of li-ion cells, taking into account the wire-bond losses. Simulation was performed in MATLAB Simulink and the simulated results were verified with hardware results obtained using a li-ion battery cycler.

articleTitle: A Comparative Investigation of Double Active Bridge Converters and Isolated Boost Mode Full Bridge Converters for Bidirectional Energy Harvester Interface applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The isolated dc-dc converter along with energy storage is becoming a promising solution in versatile applications including renewable energy based micro grids, solid state transformers, hybrid electric vehicles, fuel cell and so on. Bi-directional power flow capability and galvanic isolation are considered as prime requirements of a Bi-directional Energy Harvester Interface (BEHI). This paper presents operational principles, simulation/implementation and comparison of an isolated BEHI using Double Active Bridge (DAB) and Isolated Boost Mode Full Bridge (IBMFB) configurations.

articleTitle: Identifying Texting Idiolects using Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Nowadays internet anonymity has turned into a head-scratcher issue for most law enforcement agencies. As the technological developments in the digital field are still rising exponentially so are cyber crimes. In cyber forensics, digital profiling of anonymous tweets is done by analysing and comparing the suspect’s tweets texting idiolects the anonymous author’s writing style. Hence our project proposal is to develop a model using transformers and natural language processing (NLP) techniques for identifying the author of the anonymous chat.

articleTitle: Frequency Stability Enhancement in Solar PV System using Fractional Order Controllers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The advantages of renewable energy sources like low carbon emission, sustainability, energy security and economic development encourages the use of distributed energy resources. As the renewable energy share increases, the system stability will become an issue. This work analyses the frequency stability enhancement of the solar PV assisted system using deloading technique and different types of noninteger controllers. The system is simulated for three cases, sudden change in load, high penetration and bad weather condition. The fractional order controllers improves the dynamic performance of the system. The simulation is done using MATLAB FOMCON toolbox. The controller parameters are optimized using Particle swarm optimization algorithm.

articleTitle: RISWMCI: Robust Imperceptible Semi-blind Watermarking Scheme for Medical Color Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Color medical images are widely used in medical diagnosis for e-healthcare applications, and preserving their integrity and authenticity is a big problem. This paper presents a robust and imperceptible semi-blind color medical image watermarking scheme, which can be used for e-healthcare applications. The method uses a hybrid technique using Discrete Cosine Transform-Lower Upper factorization. The performance is evaluated using different assessment matrices for various test color images from distinct modalities. The method obtained an average PSNR of 51.99 dB, an SSIM of 0.9991, and an NC of an ideal value of 1. Its average embedding and extraction time are 0.3435 seconds, and 0.2223 seconds, respectively. The approach performs well in all respects when compared to cutting-edge methods.

articleTitle: Design of INS aided receiver integrity monitoring algorithm (ARIM) for GNSS integrated navigation systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: This paper describes the design of INS Aided Receiver Integrity Monitoring (ARIM) algorithm for GNSS integrated navigation systems. Inertial navigation systems typically use navigation grade accelerometers and gyroscopes for high reliability applications such as launch vehicles. Usage of GNSS receivers along with low cost IMUs with their measurements instances synchronized provides feasibility of realizing low-cost integrated navigation systems without compromising in performance or reliability. While the usage of GNSS receiver helps to overcome the inaccuracies caused by low cost IMU, the output of the inertial navigation system can also be used for validating the measurements taken by the GNSS receiver especially during spoofing scenarios. Validation of pseudorange measurements in this manner gives computational advantage over the conventional RAIM (Receiver Autonomous Integrity Monitoring) algorithm. The test results are a good indication of the usefulness of the algorithm in different scenarios where measurement errors are possible. In summary, ARIM algorithm presented in this paper provides an effective scheme for validating GNSS pseudorange and deltarange measurements under different possible error scenarios including spoofing and improves the overall reliability of the GNSS integrated navigation system.

articleTitle: Energy Management for Single Machine Permanent Magnet Linear Generator (PMLG) for Stand-Alone Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: This article proposes a novel operation and control scheme for a wave energy system intended for standalone use. The suggested system comprises a battery storage system, loads, and a wave energy conversion (WEC) system. The battery energy management and power regulation are at the highest level. This system generates reference dynamic operating points, which is damping and stiffness value, to regulate the power flow of the WEC system at the DC-link terminal based on state of charge of the battery. To prevent a system blackout when there is insufficient energy storage, and adverse wave circumstances, the energy management and power regulation system also controls the inverter load operation. A MATLAB/Simulink implementation of the suggested control system is used to test it under various study circumstances. The findings are displayed and discussed.

articleTitle: Space Vector Pulse Density Modulation Scheme for Multilevel Inverters using Line Voltages Coordinate Transformation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: This paper proposes a Space Vector Pulse Density Modulation (SVPDM) scheme that utilizes line voltage coordinate transformation. The scheme uses three first order Sigma Delta Modulators (SDM) for generating pulse density modulation, wherein the reference vector is vector quantized to generate the output switching vectors. The switching vectors for the inverters are derived without sector identification in this scheme making the algorithm computationally simpler. Voronoi region in the proposed Space Vector Quantizer (SVQ) are defined as a triangle with the inverter switching vectors as its vertices. The proposed SVPDM scheme retains the advantages over Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation (SVPWM) scheme such as avoidance of pulse width problem, calculation of duty ratio, use of look-up table. SVPDM has better spectral characteristics, ease of digital implementation, decreased electromagnetic interference, avoidance of complex timing calculations, and less acoustic noise of motor. The proposed scheme is simulated for a 5L Active Neutral Point Clamped (5L-ANPC) topology and result are verified.

articleTitle: An Improved Fault Identification and Location Prediction Method for AC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The idea of a microgrid is used to actively encourage the usage of distributed energy resources (DERs) to reduce the load on the power grid that relies on fossil fuels. However, the dynamic behaviour of microgrid systems under faulty conditions makes adaptive protection a general requirement for reliable microgrid operation. Therefore, identification and exact fault location prediction are essential for the system to isolate and recover from faults quickly, ensuring smooth microgrid control and operation. This paper presents an improved fault identification and fault location prediction method for AC microgrids. First, a Support Vector Machine(SVM) Classifier is used in the developed microgrid to detect the fault class and faulted line section. Subsequently, Support Vector Regression (SVR) is used to predict the precise fault point in the detected line section. Experiments with different fault conditions validate the efficacy of the proposed methodology at various locations in an IEEE 9-bus meshed AC microgrid developed in the SIMULINK platform.

articleTitle: LIDAR Based Landing Site Identification and Safety Estimation For Inter Planetary Missions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Development of the real time landing site identification and safety estimation technology is of much importance for the exploration of extraterrestrial bodies. LiDAR has become a vital element in such system due to its high accuracy, good object detection and distance estimation capability and ability to operate under any illumination condition. In this paper a LiDAR based landing site identification and safety estimation technique for inter planetary missions is proposed. A two step approach is proposed in this work. Initial coarse estimation by means of outlier detections. Fine estimation by means of landing safety assessment by computing roughness and slope within the vehicle parameter. The data is regularized by re-gridding the data and the outlier is eliminated by setting a threshold value; closely spaced outliers are identified as potential hazards like rocks, craters. K nearest neighbour interpolation is used for filling the elevation values where outliers located. Thin Plate Spline (TPS) interpolation is used for surface reconstruction. The gradient value of a TPS surface and the original surface are used to estimate slope. The residual between the surface recreated using TPS and the filtered Digital Elevation Model is used to calculate roughness. Final risk map in the landing site is the combination of the slope and roughness map. The validation of the algorithms are done using data collected by an Aerial Laser Scanner(ALS).

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Beamforming Architecture for Ultrasound Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Ultrasound imaging is used for accurate diagnosis by medical practitioners. With the developments in research and techniques, several limitations of beamforming techniques have been minimized. High contrast resolutions are required for determining organ boundaries, but there will be some constraints. Due to its simplicity, delay and sum (DAS) beamforming is used in ultrasound (US) imaging systems for the purpose of beamforming. Delay multiply and sum (DMAS) is an advanced beamforming technique, which has the advantages over DAS in situations where finer picture details in deeper scans are needed for a proper diagnosis. However, DMAS is restricted to transducer frequencies where the generated harmonics also fall within the range of processable frequencies for the US system. The best suited beamforming might be chosen based on clinical requirements and system limitations. Factor based reconfigurable architecture (FBRA) provides reconfigurable beamforming with low reconfiguration overhead for quick selection between the DAS and DMAS beamforming schemes, with accurate precision for each imaging scenario for critical diagnosis. FBRA is simulated using Xilinx Vivado and implemented on the xc7z020clg484-1 device. In this paper, the square root operation is performed using the CORDIC IP core and pipelined non-restoring algorithm, and the results are compared. By analyzing the results, it was observed that in the architecture while using pipelined non-restoring algorithm (0.23%) the hardware utilization was reduced by 0.21% compared to CORDIC IP core (0.44%). The delay of FBRA while using pipelined non-restoring algorithm (4.037ns) was reduced by 2.858ns compared to CORDIC IP core (6.895ns).

articleTitle: Denoising Autoencoder for the Removal of Noise in Brain MR Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Medical imaging methods like X-rays, ultrasound, Computed Tomography (CT) scans and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) can show structures of the internal body in great detail. However, there is unavoidable and ubiquitous noise in images created by medical imaging equipment. The use of noise reduction methods in medical imaging has therefore become crucial. In this article, we are focusing primarily on eliminating noise from MRI images of the brain. In terms of revealing details about the location and size of tumors, MRI is quite effective. Here we are proposing a Convolutional Denoising Autoencoder for removing noise from these images. Convolutional autoencoders can gently extract the data while preserving the spatial information of the image data. As a result, we can denoise with greater accuracy while using less computation and data. Our model got an SSIM value of 0.85 and a PSNR value of 30 dB.

articleTitle: Configurable Synthesizer For DWR Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Doppler Weather Radar (DWR) systems operates in S, C and X Band depending on geography and operational range. Synthesizer is a critical module in DWR system which is functional in multiple bands. The paper discusses about configurable synthesizer module which can work in S-band and L-Band with change in footprint compatible filters and software up-gradation. The module can be reconfigured and re-used for S-Band, C–Band and X-Band application. Along with adaptability, it should meet ultra-low phase noise requirements as well, which dictates performance of Radar to detect slow moving targets. The developed synthesizer module meets the system requirement of spurious suppression, phase noise and power requirement. Frequency controls, command and status exchanged over the high speed Ethernet protocol. Programmable and modular approach makes it SWaP (Size, weight, Power and Cost) synthesizer for DWR Systems.

articleTitle: Fault Detection Classification and Identification in PV Array
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: In a Photovoltaic (PV) array, the occurrence of string-to-string faults and string-to-ground faults are difficult to diagnose. In this paper two simple and robust methods of fault identification is proposed to detect the fault occurrence. Moreover the proposed fault finding algorithms can classify the three important types of electrical short circuit faults. In addition these technique can be used for all types of PV array ranging from few watts to mega watt range. The proposed methods can detect faults of any mismatch level and size of the PV array by using either two current sensors or two voltage sensors per string. One algorithm is developed for system without blocking diodes and other with blocking diodes. Both the algorithms are tested in PSIM software and analysis is detailed in this paper.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of Distributed DoS Attack by Multiple HTs in TCMP Architectures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Tiled Chip Multicore Processors (TCMP) with packet switching Network-on-Chip (NoC) have become a common method for on-chip connectivity. The performance of the entire system may suffer if a malicious Hardware Trojan (HT) is present in the NoC routers as it might negatively disrupt communication between tiles. Detecting Trojans in complicated multi-processor System on Chips (SoCs) using traditional pre and post silicon validation approaches is a huge difficulty. In this paper the presence of multiple HTs in the routing unit is modelled and its impact analysis is done for both synthetic traffic and real benchmarks using gem5 simulator. It can be observed that the presence of multiple trojans decrease the overall performance of the system.

articleTitle: Ascent Trajectory Optimization of Launch Vehicle Using Controlled Random Search
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Ascent trajectory optimization is the process of finding optimal trajectory of a launch vehicle during its ascent to space. Optimization problem involves maximising or minimising various objective functions while satisfying various constraints. In this paper, we are designing an optimal trajectory of a launch vehicle during the ascent phase to minimise the fuel consumption and to obtain maximum velocity at desired altitude using controlled random search (CRS). The ascent trajectory optimization is then compared with Random Search (RS). RS generates random points within the defined bounds for the control variables and selects the one which has highest function value, while in CRS, the algorithm generates new points by adding a random perturbation to the worst point, rather than generating completely new random points. By comparing RS and CRS, we can find which trajectory optimization method is efficient. The simulation results highlights the significant performance improvement of CRS.

articleTitle: A Novel Torque Control Scheme with Reduced Computation for Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Model Predictive Torque Control (MPTC) has been proposed as an effective alternative to conventional direct torque control (DTC) for induction motor (IM) drives. Compared to DTC, MPTC is more effective and accurate in the vector selection by incorporating the system model directly with the finite switching states. Higher calculation burden and weighting factor selection are the main disadvantages of the conventional system. In this paper, a novel method is proposed in which the number of switchings is reduced, the calculation burden is reduced and the cost function is changed in such a way that the weighting factor selection process can be avoided.

articleTitle: Microwave Imaging Technique for Detection of Low-Density Contaminants in Packaged Food
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Despite the food industry’s long and tedious efforts to eliminate risks in packaged products, some contaminants may sometimes be able to evade the controls. Low-density materials like plastics cannot be detected using common techniques, including X-Ray Imaging, Metal Detection, and Near-Infrared Imaging. A different approach that can address these drawbacks is Microwave Imaging Technology. In this work, Vector Network Analyzer was used to measure the scattering parameters to detect the presence and nature of contaminants in the food item. This detection method has the advantage of making quick and precise measurements which are very critical factors to ensure quality in the food industry.

articleTitle: Reswave-Net: A wavelet based Residual U-Net for Brain Tumour Segmentation and Overall Survival Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: A brain tumour is an abnormality in brain tissue that may cause harm to the nervous system and in severe cases can lead to death. Being a disease with a high mortality rate, the detection and accurate segmentation of brain tumour sub-regions is a crucial task in the disease diagnosis and treatment procedure. The manual segmentation process requires anatomical knowledge, is expensive, time-consuming, and inaccurate due to human errors. So, automatic and reliable segmentation methods are required; however, the large spatial and structural variability among brain tumours make automatic segmentation a challenging problem. This work proposes Reswave-Net, a deep learning network using an encoder-decoder (U-Net) architecture with residual connections to automate and standardize the task of tumour segmentation, which also incorporates wavelet decomposition of the input images. The network is trained and evaluated on Brain Tumour Segmentation (BraTS) Challenge-2020 dataset and achieves a mean Dice Score of 87.36%, 70.45%, and 72.55% and the Hausdorff distance of 6.87, 34.16 and 23.42 for the whole tumour, enhancing tumour and tumour core, respectively. For overall survival prediction, a random forest model is used where the radiomic features extracted from the image and age of the subject are used for training. The model achieves an accuracy of 58.4%.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation for Adaptive Control of a Flexible Launch Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: A Launch vehicle (LV) can carry a payload from the earth’s surface to outer space, such as spacecraft. Long range flights require high thrust-to-weight and length-to-diameter ratios in launch vehicles. This vehicle geometry results in flexible behaviour of LV which leads to instability and degradation in the systems performance. Autopilot system in the onboard computer controls the launch vehicle to fly along a predetermined trajectory along with stabilization of the rigid body and higher frequency flexible modes of the vehicle. Generally, classical control methods are used to design an autopilot, assuming the vehicle parameters to be constant over a short period of time (termed as time-slice approach).In reality, the vehicle parameters are varying due to the depletion of the propellant during the course of flight. Also the change in the environmental parameters influences the vehicle behaviour. In several scenario, classical control design may not be capable to cater the unexpected variations in the vehicle parameters. This necessitates the development of an adaptive controller which adapts to the parameter variations during the flight. For the development of an adaptive controller the estimation of parameter variations are necessary. The parameter estimator for the MIT (Massachusetts Institute of Technology) rule based adaptive controller for flexible launch vehicle (FLV) is developed in this paper.

articleTitle: Adaptive Neural Attitude and Altitude Control of a Quadrotor UAV with External Disturbances via Sliding Mode Control
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Attitude and altitude control of a quadrotor UAV is designed under time-varying external disturbances using an adaptive sliding mode control (ASMC) integrated with a neural network (NN) algorithm. The dynamic model of the quadrotor is computed considering exterior disturbances and parametric variations. A neural network algorithm combined with adaptive sliding mode control is employed to alleviate the chattering effect, and hence improve system performance. The gain parameters of sliding surfaces are accommodated with a backpropagation algorithm. The external disturbance estimation is obtained by using a disturbance observer (DO) which is incorporated with an adaptive sliding mode control. The stability of the proposed control technique is validated using the Lyapunov theory. The performance of the proposed adaptive sliding mode control using a neural network has been assessed and analyzed with other control methods using numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Deep Learning Models for Computer Generated Image Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: With the advancement in digital image processing technology, there is a huge proliferation of computer-generated images. They are widely used in interactive games, film industry and cartoons. Computer-generated images are photo-realistic because they are created using complex algorithms and high-end graphics processing power to accurately mimic real-world objects and environments’ lighting, textures, and colors. Since computer-generated images are more realistic, even human eyes can barely distinguish them. So verifying image authenticity and differentiating computer-generated images from photographic images are inevitable. This paper investigates the performance of different deep learning models for detecting computer-generated images. We experiment on three datasets: DSTok, Columbia PRCG and Rahmouni. Experimental results show that the hybrid Xception ensemble outperforms the state-of-the-art methods and achieves the highest accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score and specificity on three benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: Embedded System Based Intelligent Anti-Troxler Headlamp
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The conventional headlamp consists of a body of lights and simple optics to direct the light onto the road. Using high beams at night may cause discomfort to the other drivers on the road. This may lead to accidents. The Intelligent Anti Troxler Headlamps modulate the light throw of the projector headlamps with the help of vision sensors, spatial light modulators and object detection. This can be made possible with the advancements in machine learning as well as the advancements in the field of spatial light modulations. Object detection and image processing will be carried out on the Nvidia Jetson Nano kit. This increases the visibility of the driver and eliminates the glare which causes discomfort to the other drivers on the road due to the headlamps.

articleTitle: Facial Emotion Recognition based on Attentive Neural Network for the Blind
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Facial expressions are considered to be a universal form of nonverbal communication. They convey countless emotions without even saying a word. These cues support speech by assisting the listener in deciphering the intended meaning of the words spoken. Unfortunately, due to the absence of access to such signs for the blind and visually impaired people (VIPs), interpersonal communication is hampered. For tackling this, a deep learning-inspired Facial Emotion Recognition (FER) model that recognizes facial emotions in real-time is proposed in this paper.
