The proposed Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model was evaluated on the popular facial emotion recognition dataset of FER2013 using different performance evaluation metrics. Additionally, showcased it as a web application that runs the FER model in real-time to provide audio feedback to the visually impaired to interpret respective emotions.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Digital Wireless Communication System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The primary aim of a communication system is to transmit data reliably and efficiently. But the traditional communication systems that try to achieve this objective have their own limitations. Several research works are going on in this field that incorporate deep learning for communication systems to address the current problems. In this paper, we look into one such deep learning model called the autoencoders. Autoencoder based communication system using dense neural networks is constructed and its efficiency is evaluated by comparing the BER-SNR plots of our model to that of various theoretical, uncoded and coded traditional modulation schemes. The behaviour of the model is studied in detail to help pave the way for future researches.

articleTitle: Comparison of Load Forecasting Algorithm for Industrial Loads
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: One of the most crucial steps in the real-time management of energy production and effective energy management systems is load forecasting. Short-term load forecasting requires decisions to be made quickly and with little margin for error. This paper relies on machine learning models for the prediction of load demands. The objective of this study is to compare the effectiveness of the two-machine learning algorithms, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Auto- Regressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA). The error values of individual algorithms are compared to determine the better ML algorithm in terms of accuracy. Four parameters suchas RMSE, MAPE, MSE, and MAE are considered. From the above parameters, it is concluded that ARIMA gives better results compared to LSTM.

articleTitle: Design of Path Tracking Control and Flying Ad-hoc Network Rejoin Policy in Multi-UAV System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Multi-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) systems have shown several benefits over single UAV systems such as increased efficiency to perform tasks simultaneously, redundancy, and improved decision in case of collecting data and environmental information. There are multiple challenges in designing such systems. One of them is communication between multiple drones as it requires a reliable and robust system to ensure that the drones can communicate effectively with each other and with the operator. In this paper, we focused on designing a path-tracking control algorithm and a policy for a disconnected UAV to rejoin its network. For the path-tracking control problem, we propose a smooth control strategy based on higher-order sliding mode control. A look-up table-based network rejoin policy is proposed for the disconnected UAV. Using the Lyapunov stability criteria, it has been shown that the proposed control scheme is stable. Matlab-based numerical simulation is performed to validate the proposed combined strategy of path-tracking and rejoin policy for multi-UAV systems.

articleTitle: Coordinated Charging of Electric Vehicles for Load Levelling in Power Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The integration of electric vehicles (EVs) into the distribution network has both positive and negative impacts on the network. Due to the uncoordinated charging of EVs, there is uncertainty in the generation and load curve of the grid. This can be managed by using EVs as a source as well as a load. In this work, an optimized charge/discharge schedule of EVs connected to charging ports is proposed for load levelling with a time-of-use (TOU) tariff. The time of a day is divided into peak, off-peak, and mid-peak hours based on the forecasted load at a particular time. According to the state of charge (SOC) of batteries, EVs are classified into discharging, non-critical, critical, and highly-critical EVs. The test system selected is an IEEE 14 bus distribution system. IBM ILOG C-PLEX Optimization Studio is used as the optimization tool. The optimum values of the charging and discharging powers of EVs, power generation, and banked solar energy required for charging highly-critical EVs during peak and mid-peak hours are determined using the optimization problem. A comparative analysis between charging and discharging prices using a flat tariff, TOU tariff, and Average Power Purchase Cost (APPC) is also presented.

articleTitle: Algebraic topology as an analytic tool to check lossless nature of geometric algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Geometric representation/compression is the process of representing data as points on nonlinear spaces such as manifolds. Geometric representation algorithms for video/image data have gained significant attention in the past decade due to their ability to eliminate redundant information for storage and classification. This work presents the novel idea of using algebraic topology to decide whether a particular geometric com-pression algorithm or data representation algorithm is lossless. A necessary condition required for the compression to be lossless is derived by using the shape (topology) of the space on which compressed frames reside. The fundamental group functor is used to formulate the necessary condition as an algebraic condition which is much easier to work with. Finally, I demonstrate how the proposed idea can be utilized in a more specific setting to draw conclusions regarding a geometric algorithm’s lossless nature.

articleTitle: Removal of EOG and EMG artifacts from EEG signals using blind source separation methods
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Artifacts in EEG signals may be referred to as a disturbance in the EEG recordings that does not derive from the brain. EEG recording is in the millivolt range, and it includes the electrical activity from the muscles under the scalp. This recording often includes the artifacts due to power source, electrode movement, eyes movement, muscle movements, electrode pop, and sweating. This paper mainly concentrates on the artifacts which occurs during the eyes and muscle movement. In the proposed work, different BSS methods like FastICA, WASOBI, and EFICA algorithms are used to compare the reduction of artifacts in terms of MSE and PSNR in EEG signal. Different combinations using FastICA, WASOBI, and EFICA are evaluated and compared their performance to find the best COMBI method. Among the COMBI methods, the EFICA-WASOBI combination provides low MSE and high PSNR value, which indicates the high artifact reduction. In EFICA-WASOBI, the average value of MSE and PSNR are 0.021 and 42.78dB respectively for EMG artifact reduction and 0.060 and 32.97dB for EOG artifacts reduction using EEGdenoiseNet dataset. Similarly, the average MSE value is 0.018 and average PSNR value is 49.19dB for EOG artifact reduction using Mendeley dataset. The results show that by using the combination of EFICA-WASOBI, the effect of EOG and EMG artifacts can be reduced.

Author Keywords: Weight Adjusted Second Order Blind Identification (WASOBI)

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Classification for DC Microgrid using Binary Classification Models
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a current and current derivative based fault detection and fault classification scheme. Current and current derivatives are taken and is processed through a binary classification based machine learning(ML) algorithm. A comparative study is done between binary classification models like Decision Tree, Naive Bayes and KNN algorithms. MATLAB/SIMULINK is used to simulate a 380 V DC Microgrid(DCMG). Fault classification is done for pole-pole(PP) and pole-ground(PG) faults under different fault resistances and varying load conditions.

articleTitle: Friction Estimation of Electromechanical Actuator based Flex Nozzle Control System using Firefly Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Thrust vector controlling in space systems are carried out by Flex Nozzle Control systems. The system comprises of submerged nozzle which is connected to the main motor through a flexible joint and can be aimed in all directions with the help of actuation systems. Flex Nozzle Control (FNC) integrated with Electromechanical Actuators (EMAs) are used to aim the rocket nozzle for unerring steering of a launch vehicle.But EMAs shows certain non linear behaviour due to the frictional effects like stiction and coulomb friction, bringing down the overall system performance. To enhance the performance system should be compensated for its non linearity. It is important to first estimate the value of unknown friction present in the system. Instead of the complicated analytical methods we can use the natural algorithms which incorporate large spaces to obtain accurate results at more ease. In this work, Fire fly Algorithm is proposed to estimate the friction so as to provide suitable compensation. The proposed scheme is implemented in MATLAB/SIMULINK.

articleTitle: PAPR reduction in LFDMA systems using Modified Selective Mapping
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: High Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR) is a severe issue for single-carrier frequency division multiple access (SC-FDMA) systems, limiting it to a few applications. Selective Mapping (SLM) is a well-known PAPR reduction method that provides improved PAPR performance without signal distortion. To minimize the PAPR of Localized FDMA (LFDMA) signals for uplink transmission, a Modified Elephant Herding Optimization algorithm based SLM (MEHO-SLM) strategy is proposed in this paper. The improved method will address the optimization of phase rotation factors multiplied by the LFDMA sub-blocks in a typical SLM methodology, which is a combinatorial optimization challenge. A detailed investigation is performed to validate the effectiveness of the suggested method. The performance of MEHO-SLM-LFDMA system utilizing Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (QPSK) and Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM) schemes is compared to known optimization approaches in terms of Bit Error Rate (BER) and PAPR. The simulation results indicate that the proposed MEHO-SLM-LFDMA method will provide superior performance compared to the existing techniques while requiring less computational time.

articleTitle: Design, Implementation and Performance Assessment of Switchable Tracking Loop Filters for Ultra High Dynamic NavIC/GNSS Receiver
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Tracking loop design is one of the most important design part of NavIC/GNSS receiver design. The tracking loop determine the dynamics of the receiver. When the high dynamic receiver design is attempted, the noise bandwidth of the tracking loop filter has to be essentially increased for meeting high acceleration and jerk specifications. However the increased bandwidth causes inferior performance in navigation parameters. The stringent accuracy specifications of the receiver may not be met at lower dynamics/near static condition if tracking loop is designed for ultra high dynamics. So a switchable tracking loop is designed which select the noise bandwidth of the tracking loop filter (filter coefficients) from a set of available bandwidth options. When the receiver starts its operations, the filter bandwidth for ultra high dynamics will be chosen as default option. Once first fix is achieved, the receiver dynamics is measured and the tracking loop will be switched to required region of dynamics. Further when the dynamics changes, continuous switching of tracking loop is attempted. The tracking loop with switchable filters are implemented and performance evaluation is completed for different dynamic conditions. The algorithms are originally developed for NavIC receiver, but is applicable for receiver operates for any GNSS constellations including GPS and GALILEO. The design details of third order tracking loop for high dynamic receiver is detailed in this paper along with the design of different filters for meeting the static condition to 25km/s velocity with 20g acceleration and 20g/s jerk. The performance assessment of the the switchable tracking loop at different dynamics (using sky signal and simulated signal using GNSS constellation simulator) is completed and is presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Extraction of Actionable Threat Intelligence from Dark Web Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Darknet has emerged as an excellent platform for cybercriminals to conduct various illicit activities such as operating a fully functional crypto-currency-based marketplace or maintaining a highly anonymous communication channel. However, it also acts as a source of Cyber Threat Intelligence which is the information about the techniques, tactics, or motives of an emerging threat. The life cycle of a Darknet-based Cyber Threat Intelligence solution mainly consists of the Collection, Processing, Analysis, and Production of Data from the Darknet. The Collection and Processing stages deal with accumulating information from various dark web pages and transforming the data into some format using a big data system. The Analysis part is integral to the Threat Intelligence schema since it constitutes the extraction of named entities like Organization, Offensive Activity, Tools, etc., and the determination of relationships between these entities. The production stage is like data mining where some knowledge is extracted that can be relevant to an organization under consideration. Such knowledge can mitigate risks and disrupt any targeted cyber-attack campaigns, making Cyber Threat Intelligence actionable. In this research, an open-source-intelligence toolset is used to scan and collect data from the dark web forums through crawling and scrapping. The collected data is then ingested into a state-of-the-art NLP model that extracts actionable threat intelligence using Named Entity Recognition. The experimental results indicate that the model could identify HackerIds, tools, software, organizations, and other entities in the discussions of dark web forums with better efficiency and accuracy. This could be used to identify the source of a data leak, the release of new malware, evidence of a new exploit, and other offensive activities.

articleTitle: Virtual Modelling and Loss Study of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor used in Electric Pickup Truck
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EV) are getting common nowadays. Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSM) are one of the widely employed motors in EV applications. High power density, efficiency, compact size etc make them an excellent candidate for EV propulsion. The paper discusses design, virtual modeling and loss study of a PMSM, used in an electric pickup truck, using Ansys Maxwell.

articleTitle: Damping Control for Heaving Wave Energy Converters Using Maximum Power Point Tracking Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The purpose of this study was to evaluate damping control utilizing various maximum power point tracking (MPPT) approaches for heaving wave energy converters (WEC). A DC–DC boost converter was used to implement damping control. A perturb and observe approach was used to find the duty cycle for the MPPT. The optimal performance index for the MPPT is determined by this assessment study, along with the appropriate position for the observation parameters. The observing parameters were assessed and evaluated in three locations (electrical variables at the load, electrical variables between the source and the load, and mechanical variables near the source). According to the findings, the MPPT strategy performs the best when considering the characteristics between the source and load, and using power maximization as the performance metric.

articleTitle: Vehicle to Grid operation of an Electric Vehicle using Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: By 2025 all the existing vehicles will be completely replaced by Electric Vehicles(EV) globally. Every year automotive industry introduces EVs with new features. An onboard charger with bidirectional capability makes EVs an energy storage unit. Vehicle-to-grid operation(V2G) of an EV is a promising solution for load frequency control problems. In this work Model Predictive Control(MPC) based V2G operation is proposed. In the proposed work a three-phase Active Front End(AFE) converter(AC-DC converter) with bidirectional capability is used for designing an Onboard charger. Here the optimal discrete operation of the AFE converter is based on finding desired switching states using the MPC. By using the proposed method the power converter will maintain unity power factor, sinusoidal input current, and low voltage ripple. Simulations are done using Matlab/Simulink and the results prove the efficacy of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Challenges and software design modifications in GNSS Receiver for tackling signal strength variations under High Rate Conditions for ISRO’s re-entry Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receivers have become a de-facto standard in all launch vehicles/re-entry vehicles globally for precise navigation applications. ISRO’s launch vehicle Navigation, Guidance and Control (NGC) system also houses an indigenously developed GNSS receiver capable of acquiring GPS and NavIC satellite signals and generating position, velocity and timing (PVT) information. Launch Vehicle (LV) GNSS receivers are generally designed for high dynamic applications with high acceleration, velocity and jerk requirements. These are defined in terms of linear dynamic specifications. The challenge in designing a GNSS receiver for re-entry vehicles is to tackle high rotational body rates which can result in reduced satellite signal strength as well as loss of satellite visibility. This paper describes the challenges and software design improvements done in GNSS Receiver for tackling signal strength variations under High Rate Conditions for ISRO’s re-entry vehicles.

articleTitle: Frequency Stabilization in a Microgrid Cluster Using Plug-in Electric Vehicle with Power-Frequency Droop Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: A microgrid brings together a number of distributed energy resources, energy users and energy storing devices to supply reliable power to the end-users. It can better associate to connect to rural areas where it is not feasible and economic for a transmission system to supply power. The microgrids can be connected to form a microgrid cluster for better reliability of power when the microgrid units increase in number. The frequency of the system gets affected when the share of distributed resources increases and a plug-in electric vehicles (PEV) can be used to regulate the frequency as it can work as a generator or load. The ancillary service of a PEV in the frequency stabilization has a better response characteristics as the charging and discharging of a PEV is not a mechanical process.The accommodation of a PEV in load frequency control is possible because of the application of it in the vehicle to grid mode. The control signals are carried through communication network provided for the purpose. In a load frequency control loop with PEV, this causes time delay and hence data missing may happen. The load frequency control is greatly affected by the presence of time delay.

articleTitle: An Indigenous 32 Bit Pipelined Processor for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: In this paper, we present an indigenous 32-bit five stage pipelined processor designed and developed for future ISRO missions. The processor is a RISC processor based on IEEE 1754 instruction set architecture. It has a IEEE 754 compliant floating point unit, 1553B bus protocol controllers, timers, precise trap handler and internal memory. The processor is fabricated in 180 nm CMOS technology at Semiconductor Laboratory, Chandigarh at a frequency of 210 MHz external clock.

articleTitle: Energy-efficient Data Aggregation Schemes for Low-power Distributed Wireless Sensor Networks using Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The advancements in distributed computing and technologies such as Industry 4.0 have rapidly deployed wireless sensor networks. In many scenarios, battery-connected wireless sensors gather the surrounding information that is to be aggregated at a base station. The volume of data generated from large-scale wireless networks has significant impacts on storage, network latency, and bandwidth. This demands efficient data aggregation systems for new-generation smart networks. Compressed sensing techniques are proven to deliver efficient compression for sparse signals. This paper evaluates the extension of such compression techniques to distributed low-power wireless sensor networks for efficient data aggregation.

articleTitle: Fourth Order Sliding Mode Control of Position for Electro-Hydraulic Actuator
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: A control method for the accurate tracking of position of an Electro-Hydraulic actuation system is presented in this paper. The Electro-Hydraulic state space model of the system is derived from the fundamental equations of an actuator. A second order demodulator is used to obtain the output position feedback of the system. Because of the insensitivity to parameter variations and uncertainties, the sliding mode algorithm is recognized as an effective technology for the design of robust controllers. Hence, a sliding mode technique is adopted to control the position of the system to follow the desired command signal. Since, the relative degree of the system with respect to position is four, a universal control law which is developed explicitly for SISO systems with higher relative degrees has been used known as the 4 - Sliding Mode Control. The control system developed is proposed to minimize the tracking error as the position feedback follows the reference command. The effectiveness of the proposed control algorithm is validated by simulations carried out on the system. The results are then compared with a traditional PI controller and a Lag compensator in cascade with a roll-off filter which further shows the beneficial effects of the proposed 4 - SMC.

articleTitle: Shunt Active Power Filter for Single Phase Low Voltage Distorted Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The power quality of low voltage distribution system is greatly affected with the harmonic pollution due to the penetration of power-electronic loads. Harmonic compensation is achieved using shunt active filters at the point of common coupling. Shunt active filters injects harmonic current required by load making source current sinusoidal. In distorted voltage networks, this method is not suitable since it reduces the power factor of system. This paper proposes a modified control algorithm based on resistive load synthesis. The proposed method is analysed by performing simulation in MATLAB Simulink. The control algorithm identifies source harmonic current contribution at the point of common coupling and is utilised for calculation of filter current. Simulation results point to the effectiveness of proposed method in increasing the power factor of the system.

articleTitle: A Survey on Integration of Blockchain in Data Trading Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: With the development of computer and information technology, diverse types of data are being created daily. This data along with big data technologies could give a lot of useful information when used right. To make this possible, many data trading platforms exist now. But since these systems are based on a third party platform who collect and trade data, there are many privacy and security concerns. To solve these problems, blockchain technology have been being proposed. The decentralised and transparent nature of blockchain could help to solve many security concerns. In this work, we provide a survey on data trading systems which utilize blockchain as the primary entity for trust-enabling to avoid any intermediaries. We provide an overview of blockchain technology and discuss the working and limitations of the centralized data trading systems. Also, we provide insights into DApp and Ethereum blockchain.

articleTitle: OCT Image-Based Macular Disease Classification Using Multilayer Deep Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents a technique for improved detection of macular diseases using Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) images. The method combines two pre-trained CNN models, VGG16 and InceptionV3, to form a Deep Feature Fusion of CNN that can effectively detect retinal abnormalities in Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) images. The model adaptively and explicitly fuses lower and upper layer activations to achieve better results than traditional fully connected layer features. Test results show improved performance on public databases of retinal OCT images.

articleTitle: IoT Based Smart Parking System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The number of vehicles being used for daily commute within the cities have increased exponentially since 2015. This has caused a major concern regarding parking spaces especially in a rapidly developing cities. More than 25% of vehicles driving around the cities are looking for a parking space. Numerous issues arise as a result of poor parking infrastructure such as significant wastage of time for drivers, traffic congestion and increase in car emissions. Implementing smart technology to facilitate this task will solve this problem, improving operational efficiency, simplifying the flow of urban traffic and offering drivers a more enjoyable and time-saving experience. The proposed IoT-based smart parking system allows real-time data about parking availability to be obtained via a mobile application. An IoT gadget, which includes sensors and microcontrollers is placed in each parking space. The data from the gadget will be pushed to a cloud-based system which analyses this data to calculate the availability of free slots in parking spaces. The users receive real-time information on the availability of all parking spaces giving them the choice to choose the best one.

articleTitle: Classification of leaf spot diseases in banana using pre-trained convolutional neural networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Banana is a leading fruit crop in the global market and is grown all over the world. However, its production and trade are severely affected by the diseases caused by fungi, bacte- ria and viruses. Early diagnosis and management of such diseases are essential to avoid the yield loss. This paper demonstrates a deep learning based automated algorithm for the classification of three important leaf spot diseases in banana namely, Sigatoka, Cordana and Deightoneilla. Images of banana leaves infected with these diseases have been applied to four augmented pre-trained convolutional neural networks and their performance in disease classification is compared. An accuracy of 91.7% is achieved on the model with DenseNet 121 backbone.

articleTitle: 3D Brain MRI Segmentation using Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Magnetic Resonance Images (MRI) have been utilized by radiation oncologists to identify the size of tumours within the brain.The accurate identification of brain tumours from 3D MRI images is essential for proper diagnosis. Our proposed model introduces a network capable of segmenting 3D images using sparsely labeled data. This network is an enhanced version of the u-net architecture with attention network and utilizes 3D operations, without the need for a pre-trained network. The effectiveness of this approach was evaluated on the well-known BraTS 2018 brain dataset and achieved a Dice Similarity Coefficient score of (0.95, 0.89, 0.95) for the complete, core, and enhancing regions, respectively

articleTitle: Accuracy improvement for MEMS Piezoresistive Pressure Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Accurate measurement of pressure using piezoresistive MEMS sensors requires proper quantification and correction of its errors. Algorithmic temperature compensation of such a pressure sensor gives an accuracy that is one order better than resistive-compensation, but it is a time-consuming process. This paper discusses a MATLAB-based method to extract the correction coefficients for a MEMS pressure sensor and evaluates the extent of their effectiveness before they are fed into the system and experimented in hardware. The contribution of non-linearity error is analyzed and reduced. A method to improve the match between sensors as required in some aerospace applications is also discussed.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Guide for Optimizing the switching of an Automotive Grade MOSFET in a Half-Bridge Topology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: This paper is written as a comprehensive guide to assist students and practicing engineers in optimizing a half-bridge MOSFET switching circuit used in the automotive industry with a 12V DC bus. Mathematical calculations for sizing gate resistors and gate-source capacitors, ways to avoid dv/dt-induced false turn-on of MOSFETs, and a snubber circuit for minimizing parasitic oscillation at switching nodes are presented. The entire study has been validated through LTspice simulations using a half-bridge circuit with realistic parasitics in the current path.

articleTitle: Recent Developments in Plastic Optical Fiber based Wearable Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Wearable sensors are a convenient method for monitoring human health parameters. In medical application, a number of wearable sensors have been developed to monitor different parameters like body temperature, muscle motion, heart rate, blood pressure etc. Plastic optical fiber (POF) is a suitable media for developing sensors for human parameters monitoring. The compact and light weight sensors developed by using plastic optic fiber has certain advantages compared to its counterparts. The immunity to electromagnetic interference makes fiber sensors suitable for medical instruments where other instruments are also operational in the surroundings. This paper reviews the recent developments in POF based wearable sensors.

articleTitle: Inter-Stage Relay Selection Architecture for Priority Based User Scheduling among Multiple Users using Hybrid Cuckoo Search Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The recent developments in relay assisted wireless communication have laid down significant achievement in terms of energy efficiency. The future wireless generation networks are particular about serving multiple users with maximum achievable sum-rate for individual users. The existing relay selection and optimization algorithms are targeting on multiple users without considering the priority and scheduling protocols. The target of existing relay selection algorithms is merely to maximize the overall average sum-rate. This may result in reduction of sum rate for prioritized calls, even though average sum rate has been maximized. This paper presents a novel relay selection algorithm to maximize the sum-rate for prioritized calls without reducing the overall average sum-rate using Hybrid Cuckoo Search Optimization algorithm. The proposed work claims significant improvement in Prioritized Achievable Sum-Rate for prioritized calls for different use cases.

articleTitle: An Inception based Urothelial Cell Classification Network for the detection of Bladder Carcinoma from Urine Cytology Microscopic Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Medical image diagnostics now benefit greatly from the use of deep convolutional neural networks. The CNN-based deep neural networks are extensively used in the medical classification tasks. Although deep learning algorithms have gained performance comparable to pathologists in interpreting whole slide images for the detection of tumours, very few researchers have explored the possibility of detecting urothelial carcinoma from microscopic images. In this study, we propose a novel deep learning model for urine cytology smear-based detection of urothelial cell cancer (UCC). The network is based on Inception architecture that can efficiently learn the features of varied size cells in the image and produced relatively high accuracy when compared to state-of-the-art techniques. The proposed technique is evaluated using a dataset that includes the cytology samples of 115 individuals, 59 of whom had UCC instances that were histologically confirmed and the remaining 56 benign cases were identified through routine cytology samples. The suggested approach offers 98.63% accuracy with fewer parameters. The method’s performance in terms of accuracy and parameter count is highly encouraging.

articleTitle: Fault Tolerant Model Reference Adaptive Controller for Launch Vehicle Electromechanical Actuation System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: In Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV), a Flex Nozzle Control (FNC) system, with the help of a linear actuator, is utilized to steer the launch vehicle. Electromechanical actuators (EMA) are usually preferred since they are easier to control and provides more safety. For the successful completion of a mission, control of EMA as well as the tolerance towards the failures are equally important. This paper proposes an algorithm to overcome the main issues faced by the system like parameter variations, disturbances and the failure of sensors. The controller used in this paper is Model Reference Adaptive Controller (MRAC), and the main advantage of the MRAC strategy is that it does not require the precise information about the fault location or amplitude. This paper also deals with the use of modified MIT rule for the design of MRAC. The efficacy of the proposed controller is verified through simulation results.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of Modbus serial line Server RTU VIP
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Verification is a crucial phase in the design cycle of an ASIC or FPGA. As the digital design complexity keeps increasing, its verification complexity increases as well. In this scenario, the concept of VIP (Verification intellectual property) emerged, which is a pre-packaged set of code used for verification that could be easily plugged into a simulation environment to shorten the verification cycle and increase the coverage.Modbus RTU (Remote Terminal Unit) is the serial version of Modbus data communication protocol. Modbus serial line server RTU VIP is an endeavour to optimize the efforts dispensed in a FPGA/ ASIC project implementation. The algorithm for the Modbus VIP is designed and implemented in Universal Verification Methodology. The Modbus VIP brings in automation to the cumbersome testing process and cut short the lengthy man hours spend in simulation result analysis and debugging. It addresses the challenges in the verification of a Modbus implementation in terms of functional and structural coverage, efficient bug detection, effective debugging and drastically lessen the verification effort, reduce the overall product cycle time and thereby, the product cost.

articleTitle: Lucas Kanade based Optical Flow for Vehicle Motion Tracking and Velocity Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Optical flow is a powerful application of image processing that is used in a variety of applications, primarily in object tracking and motion estimation. In this paper, we implement a system for vehicle motion tracking and velocity estimation using Lucas-Kanade (L-K) algorithm based optical flow method. The work includes two applications of optical flow: tracking the movement of the vehicle in the case of a fixed camera and velocity estimation of a vehicle with a camera mounted on it. Pre-processing steps include gaussian smoothing, and computing spatial and temporal gradients. This is followed by the further formulation of Lucas kanade equation in the form of matrices. The system of equations is then solved using the least square error criteria, and the flow vectors are obtained. Processes such as segmentation, blob analysis, camera calibration, and thresholding are further done which are used for velocity estimation as well as motion tracking. The functionality was tested and verified on video sequences obtained from the lab testing scenarios and real-world camera visuals taken from various sources.

articleTitle: An In-Depth Description of Multi-Agent Systems for Controlling Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Agents are cognitive beings that can think for themselves, operate in various contexts, and make good decisions based on their knowledge and experience. A multi-agent system (MAS) uses intelligent, interconnected agents to solve a problem that no single agent can handle. SG integrates smart technologies, control methods, and sensing methods into utility power networks. Using MAS to regulate power system operations can save time on analysis, relaying, protection, transmission switching, communication protocols, and plant control. This study examines smart grids, MAS-based control methods, and smart grid control. Twenty-five publications on MAS-based smart grid control have been analysed, categorised, and grouped for reference. This paper should help MAS researchers and practitioners.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of Underwater Image Processing based on Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Underwater image processing has been an active research topic over the past few years as interest in marine observation and the use of ocean resources has increased. Different from conventional images, marine ecosystems are frequently subjected to challenging conditions such as underwater turbulence, low contrast, and high colour distortion as a result of the light's non-uniform attenuation as it passes through the water. To overcome these challenges, a good amount of work in conventional and deep learning based underwater image processing has been published over a period of time. Deep learning has demonstrated excellent performance improvement than the conventional approaches on the challenging vision tasks. In this survey, important underwater image processing methods using deep learning have been discussed. The major underwater metrics, common datasets, and challenges are also presented.

articleTitle: Machine Learning based Vacant Space Detection for Smart Parking Solutions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Urban areas of countries around the world are plagued with parking space shortages, because of the burgeoning population of private vehicles. Lack of information on parking space availability for drivers causes the drivers to waste time searching for an off-street parking space, thereby contributing to traffic congestion. With surveillance cameras being used for security purposes, the images captured from the same can be conveniently used for the detection of vacant parking slots. This paper proposes a machine learning-based vacant space detection of vacant parking spaces. The ‘YOLO’ algorithm is used to identify the occupied parking slots by processing the images obtained from the surveillance cameras, from which the positions of vacant parking slots are derived. The output from the implementation of the YOLO algorithm is used to estimate vacant parking slots using the proposed algorithms. The proposed system is found to give very accurate estimates of the vacant slots for demarcated and non-demarcated parking lots.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Underwater Image Enhancement Using Style Transfer Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: In ocean engineering and research, underwater imaging is a developing field. Usually, underwater images exhibit low contrast, distorted colour, and blurred features due to factors like refraction, absorption, and scattering of light by water-borne suspended particles. In order to address these challenges, we have proposed a novel style transfer based deep learning approach for the enhancement of underwater images. The suggested method consists of two stages: i) segmentation stage and ii) enhancement stage. The segmentation stage is implemented using SUIM-Net, which does the semantic segmentation of underwater images. The second stage is the enhancement stage, where we use a style transfer technique, which consists of an encoder-decoder circuit with whitening and coloring transforms. It also uses wavelet pooling which preserves the structural features while stylizing the distorted underwater images. These aids in reconstructing the signals more accurately. To evaluate the performance of the suggested method, various metrics such as Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), Peak Signal to Noise Ratio (PSNR), Underwater Image Quality Measure (UIQM) and Underwater Color Image Quality Evaluation (UCIQE) are used. Better UIQM values were obtained using the suggested method when it was compared to other cutting-edge methodologies.

articleTitle: Application of Hybrid Techniques for Efficient Photovoltaic Systems-An Overview
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: In the last few decades, the application of photovoltaic (PV) systems grabs significant attention as it is one of the major promising sources of green energy. Modern advancement in PV technologies makes it well effectual and affordable in wide areas such as power generation on-grid/ off-grid system, street illumination, pumping out water in agriculture sector etc. However, the extraction of maximum power from the modules is inevitably needed for the productive utilization of PV systems. Hence, a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) mechanism is essential for optimizing net energy production. This paper encapsulated the concept of different approaches based on the intelligent mechanisms for efficient power extraction in PV systems. An extensive summary in terms of the efficiency and eventuality of the reported hybrid techniques has been discussed in detail in this work.

articleTitle: Semi-Autonomous Non-singular Terminal Sliding Mode Control of a Micro Aerial Robot for Outdoor Wall Climbing Operation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: In this work, a non-singular terminal mode sliding mode controller is developed for output tracking with unmodeled dynamics, parameter uncertainty, and constrained disturbances, allowing the micro aerial robot to climb the wall. In order to successfully eliminate chattering in control action, it is recommended to use a modified power rate reaching law. Using Lyapunov’s criterion, we demonstrate stability over finite intervals of time. The effectiveness of the suggested control for trajectory tracking and wall climbing under conditions of parametric uncertainty and disturbances is shown via simulation. The suggested controller is compared to conventional sliding mode techniques to validate the claimed decrease in chattering. The suggested control strategy for free-flight and wall-climbing operations in GPS-denied outdoor settings is validated by real-time trials with a modified Crazyflie nano-quadcopter.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Detection of ADHD using EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a neurodevelopmental irregularity which is complex, universal and heterogeneous. Inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness are some of the symptoms of ADHD. The disease is developing at preschool years and can even extend to adulthood when proper diagnosis is not provided. Hence detection of ADHD is very essential. ADHD detection can be done using EEG signal. In this review, we analysed the available research on deep and machine learning studies on diagnosing ADHD and found the various diagnostic setups that have been employed. The paper discusses the existing techniques present using different classifiers. It briefly explains the different methods when using Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) as classifier. Comparative study on these methods were done and performance measures was increased over time.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on Epilepsy Prediction Using Modern Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Epilepsy is a persistent, contagious brain condition that affects about 50 million individuals worldwide. It is characterized by repeated epilepsy, which are short lived bursts of jerking movements that can either affects the whole body or just a tiny proportion of it. The way a seizure presents itself may differ greatly among epileptics. They may differ depending on the human characteristics. If we are aware of the four stages of a seizure, we can better understand what happens in the brain during seizures. 20% of epileptics experience preictal stages, and thus, this stage may serve as initial seizure warning signs. People who went through the prodromal phase may even feel empowered during this time since they may be informed of an impending seizure. Since the embedded information in the preictal phase follows the ictal phase, it is possible to predict epilepsy in earlier from the brain waves. It alerts the doctors to the impending seizure. Seizures may be anticipated, according to multiple sources in the fields of engineering, medicine, and patent publications. Some of the seizure prediction methods include frequency-based approaches, statistical EEG signal analysis, nonlinear dynamics (chaos), and intelligently designed systems. For epilepsy prediction, there are both machine and deep learning techniques. The methods are usually categorized on the basis of which type of classifier or which type of classification technique are used for prediction. The various preictal prediction techniques and their outcomes were thoroughly discussed in this review.

articleTitle: Artificial Level Language: A Library of Computing Engine for Natural Languages*
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Programming with natural language is an area of research with different kinds of applications including introductory programming, robotics, etc. Factors like meaning preservation, ambiguity handling, etc, have to be considered while writing programs in natural language. Natural language programming is evolved over the past years through various developments. Here we introduce a system that can convert sentences written in natural language (we considered English as an example) to python statements. The main feature of our system is that the English sentences need not be grammatically correct. We named our system as Artificial Level Language (ALL) as it can be thought of as a new level, above the high-level language, in the programming language hierarchy. The main component of ALL is a tranSMachine comprised of two parts namely tranScripter and transCompiler. The tranScripter introduced here is named as JAVS-tranScripter which includes a set of protocols that are expected to be improved in the future. ALL take English statements as input and it generates Python code in the background to carry out the instructions and outputs the results.

articleTitle: Modeling and advanced control strategies for the beer fermentation process
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Beer has existed for centuries. Fermentation is necessary. Over time, fermentation techniques have evolved. Despite having identical ingredients, each beer is unique. Beer production requires a source of carbs and yeast. Microbes aid brewers from the manufacture of raw materials to packaging stability. Some people overlook beer because it is made through the fermentation of food. Esters, acids, and higher alcohols are all susceptible to the effects of temperature. Fermentation temperatures can boost acidity and fruitiness. The influence of temperature on them is modeled using MATLAB/Simulink, and the temperature profile of an industrial environment is incorporated into the resulting model. The dynamic model is used to determine appropriate controller settings for optimal control, and the PID and MPC controllers are employed to obtain recognizable temperature profiles for flavor development.

articleTitle: DeepWeight: A Semi-Autonomous Food Weight Billing System using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The manual billing process in grocery store food sections often results in long lines and inefficiency. This not only wastes time but can also discourage customers from purchasing food items. DeepWeight offers a solution to this problem by using deep learning to train a CNN model that can detect the type of food, collect weight data using a load cell, capture an image of the food using a camera, predict the type of food in the image using the model, and print a label with relevant information using a printer. This system is powered by technologies such as Python3, fast.ai, a USB camera, a load cell module, a printer, and a Raspberry Pi 3. Our model is built on the ResNet-152 architecture and achieves an accuracy of 99.22% after 5 epochs of training. Additionally, it employs a unique approach of using weight cell readings to trigger the system, rather than the conventional method of image sensing. This approach helps to reduce billing time, avoid false triggers, and improve the efficiency of grocery stores.

articleTitle: Challenges in Creating Text Summarization Models in Malayalam: A Study
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Automatic text summarization (ATS) is a task where information is being condensed for easy understanding. Malayalam text summarization is in formative state due to the bottleneck of methodologies, datasets and evaluation techniques. Deep learning is a better solution to achieve the balance between output accuracy and system complexity. Through this literature, we are probing into the fundamental aspects of building Malayalam text summarization models so as to highlight prevailing mechanisms, challenges, and future scope in the field. A comprehensive understanding of Malayalam grammatical structure and language-specific feature study has been carried out to achieve the goal. Afterward, available preprocessing tools and their deficiencies were discussed followed by prevailing text summarization mechanisms in Malayalam. Meanwhile, different datasets and evaluation strategies were inquired in order to demarcate their incapacities. This survey would give an overall insight for designing an ATS system in Malayalam, and we hope that the fellow researchers in this area would make use of this road map for literature works.

articleTitle: Multi-Class Fall Detection Based on Machine Learning by using FallAIID dataset
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The prevalence of falls among older adults is a significant concern for healthcare professionals and researchers. Preventing fall-related injuries and deaths requires accurate and efficient fall detection systems. This paper proposes a novel approach for multi-class fall detection using machine learning techniques with the FallAIID dataset, evaluates its performances, and proposes an efficient low-cost prototype hardware system. The proposed method leverages the unique characteristics of the FallAIID dataset to accurately classify different types of falls and daily activities with an accuracy of 96% for wrist-worn devices and 95% for neck and waist worn devices. The results of our evaluation demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach and its potential to improve fall detection in real-world settings.

articleTitle: Topologies used in EV charging system – A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The automobile usage around the world has been increasing rapidly in day to day life, leading to heavy increase in pollution, which further increases the greenhouse gas emissions. Due, to this as an alternative for Electric Vehicles (EVs) are preferred. The EVs uses power as their primary fuel or to boost the effectiveness of conventional vehicle models and the electric cars, also known as battery EVs or plug-in hybrid vehicles are specified as EVs (PHEVs). Since, some of these vehicles still utilize liquid fuels in addition to energy, such automobiles are commonly referred to as electric automobiles or simply EVs. There has been substantial study into EVs as a potential way for reducing the greenhouse impact. The EVs provides competitive driving range and fuel economy, compared to vehicles with a combustion engine and these are mainly due to the progressions in power appliances, battery storage, and assistance (ICEV). The effectiveness of the PHEV greatly increases with the aid of optimized control techniques or by using the idea of an energy management system. Since EVs are extremely low with carbon dioxide emissions, reduced noise, better efficiency, flexibility in grid operation and connectivity, EVs provides hope for a sustainable transportation industry in the future. An overview of electric vehicle technology, together with related systems for energy storage and charging infrastructure, is discussed in this paper. Moreover, a comparative analysis is carried out amid the different techniques used in EV charging system, in order to determine the effective technique.

articleTitle: CNN-based Cognitive Distraction Surveillance for Pedestrians using Phones and Headphones
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The use of cell phones or headphones by pedestrians is a major concern for traffic safety. It exponentially raises the likelihood of an accident occurring. Since the frequency of pedestrian fatalities caused by mobile phone or headphone usage is on the rise, authorities restrict pedestrians from using cell phones or headphones. However, in order to execute the regulation, law enforcement officials are currently stationed at the roadside to visually assess pedestrians. This method is time-consuming and ultimately ineffective. The proposed CNN-based architecture is designed to detect pedestrians who are using phones or headphones while crossing the street. The ResNet-50 model has been fine-tuned for the task using transfer learning. This detection algorithm identifies offenders and highlights them using OpenCV. The proposed algorithm identifies people, who are breaking the rules by using phones or headphones while crossing the street, with the help of an efficient and cost-effective methodology.

articleTitle: EBICS: Even Blind I Can See, A Computer Vision Based Guidance System For Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Humans have five senses that help them to interact with the environment. Even losing one makes this interaction difficult. There are more than 63 million visually impaired people in India. Visually impaired people can range from being partially impaired to completely blind. These individuals face numerous difficulties in performing daily life tasks. Fortunately, assistive technologies have developed in the last few decades. This technology aims to enable people to live a healthy and independent life with equal opportunities in society. This paper describes the visual assistive system that ensures people live their lives to the fullest. This system helps people interact with the immediate environment in which they are living while taking care of them and keeping them safe from the dangerous elements in the surrounding. The proposed system uses a Raspberry Pi camera and Raspberry Pi 4 embedded system to interact with the environment and the user. We propose to aid the visually impaired community by employing a system that allows us to identify different objects and their inter-spacing distance between the object and the individual whilst simultaneously providing audio feedback. This is achieved by capturing the real-time frames and processing these images. The proposed system boasts an accuracy of 93.7%, thus outperforming similar products while being cheaper and using fewer resources simultaneously. Unlike other devices in the market. This result was achieved with no additional sensors helping reduce the cost of the proposed system significantly and making it affordable for the general public. It also reduces the point of failure as there is no additional hardware sensors other than a camera being used.

articleTitle: Design and Cost Analysis of a Decentralized Hybrid Renewable Energy System-based Microgrid for Insular Rural Area: Hatiya of Bangladesh as an off- grid solution
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: A large number of people in Bangladesh, especially in the coastal areas, are still deprived of on-grid electricity power, especially in the country's coastal islands and hilly regions. Getting the motivation to bring them under the blessings of electric power, a design consisting of multiple renewable energy sources is proposed in this paper. Geographically, the country is located in a suitable position for exploiting renewable energy since it locates near the tropical region. This paper presents the design of a hybrid topology-based renewable energy system consisting of solar and wind power and battery support. The design is mainly proposed for the insular coastal region people. Since solar and wind powers have fluctuating natures, feedback circuit-based Multi-Input-Single-Output Single Ended Primary Inductor Converter (SEPIC) is used. The DC-DC SEPIC converter is utilized in boost mode operation. Also, batteries are connected to the system for backup as storage devices in case of gloomy weather. The topology is validated in MATLAB/Simulink environment. Moreover, the design is fed into Homer Optimization Tool with a view to justifying the technical feasibility and economic analysis. Different intermittence situations, solar irradiance, and seasonal fluctuation were also taken into consideration throughout the software assessment. The reason behind using wind and solar energy for hybridization is the lack of infrastructure to utilize hydro power and geothermal energy everywhere in Bangladesh. Although numerous earlier research works analyzed hybrid systems, this work presents a thorough techno-economic analysis of hybrid systems with backup and comprehensive simulation findings. Hatiya, a largely rural island detached from mainland Bangladesh is considered here for analysis. A small community of Hatiya is considered during the simulation in HOMER. All of the analysis is done based on the geographical position of Hatiya in this paper.

articleTitle: Investigations on Recent Advancements in the Fabrication of In-Plane Micro-Supercapacitors as Portable Energy Storage Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The recently increasing demand for portable or wearable electronic devices has called for advancements in portable and miniaturized energy storage devices. Microbatteries used for portable energy storage applications have shorter lifetime, low power density and can contain toxic constituents. Micro-supercapacitors (MSCs) are promising energy storage devices with high power density, short charge-discharge time, longer service time and contain no toxic metals or liquids. Micro-supercapacitors can be fabricated as sandwich type or planar type configuration. Planar architecture of micro-supercapacitors makes the device more flexible, decreases the ionic diffusion length and also easy on-chip integration of device compared to conventional three-dimensional architecture. The recent advancements in planar micro-supercapacitors in terms of fabrication methodology, material and architecture is reviewed in this paper.

articleTitle: State-of-the-Art Techniques For Design Of Anti-Cancer Drug Delivery System Based On Optimal Control Methods: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Cancer is a leading cause of mortality and morbidity worldwide. Approximately 700,000 cancer deaths occur annually in the United States and every year, more than a million new cancer cases are predicted. Chemotherapy and hyperthermia are effective treatment options for patients with high-risk cancers. At disseminated cancer sites, chemotherapeutic drugs can be infused into the bloodstream to stop cancer cell growth and/or spread. The dose of drugs infused into a patient's vein during chemotherapy is often controlled using computerized drug delivery systems. Clinicians typically struggle to identify the correct dosage of intravenous chemotherapy because of unforeseen side effects such as immune response and increased toxicity, and optimization algorithms and automated control approaches have been developed to aid in the safe administration of cancer chemotherapy drugs. To govern the distribution of closed-loop intravenous anticancer medicines, several controllers have been created, and numerous mathematical models have been developed to mimic the behavior of cancer by considering various phases in various treatment options such as chemotherapy and radiation. This study provides a current state-of-the-art review of the function of anti-cancer drug delivery systems, as well as the control approaches and different strategies used in building an anti-cancer drug delivery system, such as mathematical models, optimized control, and hybrid algorithms.

articleTitle: A Review on Electromagnetic Metamaterial Absorbers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Metamaterials are artificially engineered materials that possess properties that are not present naturally. They show some specific properties such as negative refractive index, negative permittivity, negative permeability and left hand behavior. Metamaterial absorbers have greater attention in nowadays because of its ability to absorb incident electromagnetic radiation. The structure consists of resonator layer, dielectric substrate and metallic ground plane. They are applicable in radar cross section reduction (RCS), energy harvesting, electromagnetic shielding and refractive index sensing. In this paper, various metamaterial absorbers and their applications are reviewed. Initially the theory and working of metamaterial absorbers are discussed. Several multiband absorbers and their absorptivity are then presented. Next, the review focuses on several broadband absorbers and polarization insensitive absorbers. By using these metamaterial absorbers, we can make near-unity absorption.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Control of a Truck Trailer Robot Using Feedback Linearization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: A truck trailer system consist of a tractor connected to the trailer by means of connecting point called hitch point. The trajectory tracking control of a tractor trailer robot with on axle hitching in both forward and backward motion is addressed in this paper. The kinematic model of the truck trailer is developed and a nonlinear controller is designed which ensures that the center point of the trailer axle follows a predefined trajectory, described by a geometric path and a velocity profile. A closed loop stabilization control by using the feedback of the states is done. A controller based on feedback linearization is used to drive the truck trailer robot through the generated trajectory to move the robot from the initial pose to the final pose. The effectiveness of the proposed controller is validated using MATLAB simulations. The simulation results of the work show that the tractor trailer robot can be effectively controlled to track the curved and linear paths by using the control law.

articleTitle: Review of Speech Enhancement Methods using Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The goal of speech enhancement is to restore the quality of noise affected speech by removing the noise. The purpose of speech enhancement is to increase the damaged speech signal’s comprehensibility and overall perceptual quality. Given the nature of the noise, which is very non-stationary, speech enhancement is a difficult challenge. In recent years, speech enhancement has been accomplished using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). This review includes GAN based speech enhancement algorithms, data sets and evaluation metrics. We also discuss the issues and compare the performance of the different speech enhancement methods.

articleTitle: FSO Challenges and Solutions at 5G Networks - A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The 5G network, another generation of phone net-works, is aimed at machine to machine connection, the Internet of Things. To support Internet of Things, 5<sup>th</sup> generation networks must not only give greater bandwidth at access points, but less latency. Because multiple equipments to be connected is came to be very high, 5<sup>th</sup> generation is expected to be an ultra dense network with large number of little cells allowing connection to houses, vehicles, humans. This necessitates strong fronthaul, backhaul connection. This review paper investigates evolving architecture for 5<sup>th</sup> generation networks, with particular emphasis on FSO links. It examines challenges in Free Space Optics communications, with focus on climate, 5G network alignment parameters. Paper also looks at solutions for upcoming these obstacles, supporting IoT, machine to machine applications over 5<sup>th</sup> generation networks.

articleTitle: Sensorless Direct Torque Control Techniques for Induction Motor Drives: A Status Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Induction motor is a type of ac motor widely used in the industry for a wide range of applications. An inverter fed induction motor constitutes an induction motor drive. Direct torque control (DTC) is a method of controlling an induction motor drive. DTC is simple to implement unlike Field oriented control (FOC) and involves the direct control of motor parameters like electromagnetic torque and flux. The advantage over other methods of control is that DTC is less sensitive to motor parameters. Sensorless DTC refers to elimination of speed sensors but instead speed estimation techniques are used to avoid the redundant hardware that adds up when sensors are used. This paper gives a status review on DTC and sensorless estimation techniques that have evolved over the course of these years.

articleTitle: Review on Video Super Resolution: Methods and Metrics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Video Super Resolution (VSR) is a wide area in image processing, where numerous research works are going on. Super Resolution (SR) means the upstaging of Low Resolution (LR) frames to High Resolution (HR) frames with minimal loss in image quality. The goal of this paper is to give the comprehensive review of various VSR methods like Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Generative Adversarial Network (GAN), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Spatial Temporal Transformer (STT), Fractional-Sine Cosine Algorithm (F-SCA), Recurrent Back-Projection Network (RBPN), Temporally-Deformable Alignment Network (TDAN). Finally, the readers will get more ideas about VSR based methods and metrics.

articleTitle: Thrust Vectoring and its Effects on Vertical Take-off and Landing of Monocopters - A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Vertical Take-off and Landing (VTOL) vehicles have evolved and progressed through the ages and have come to the level of present-day advanced drone technology. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are widely used in the modern world for numerous applications. These vehicles are basically VTOL systems that are miniature in structure and cost-effective when compared to their predecessors. This paper covers an idea on the conventional VTOL systems and modern drones which is then followed by focusing more on a lesser explored area of drones which is the monocopter, especially thrust vectoring monocopter. Monocopter has inherent advantages like small structure and lightweight. The paper also discusses different types of conventional monocopters along with their benefits and limitations. The thrust vectoring monocopter is given highlight because it has added advantage of compensating the inherent autorotation in the conventional monocopter with the help of control fins thereby building a stable cost-effective system. Hence this paper presents a comparative study on the VTOL systems, conventional monocopters and thrust vectoring monocopter.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Architectures Based Sentiment Analysis Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Recently, sentiment analysis has attracted a good deal of interest from researchers. Each day, FB, Twitter, Weibo, and other social media, in addition to huge e-trade websites, generate big feedback, which can be used to investigate humans' critiques or emotions. Sentiment analysis will correctly analyze subjective records from this information. Deep learning becomes an effective machine learning approach which learns from a couple of layers of representations or features of the records and outputs a cutting-edge prediction effect. Deep learning overcomes all other machine learning techniques for sentiment analysis as well as offers different architectures for sentiment evaluation. Recently, RNN abbreviated as Recurrent Neural Networks as well as CNN abbreviated as Convolutional Neural Networks has been replaced with Transformer Language models in deep learning architecture.This survey deals with contemporary architectures and challenges in that are in Sentiment Analysis as well as Natural Language Processing.

articleTitle: Speech Emotion Recognition, Datasets, Features and Models: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: There are several ways in which we can express our emotions, such as through our voice, body language, facial expressions, and eye contact. Speech is a crucial means of conveying our feelings and viewpoints to others, and as a result, emotions play a vital role in human communication and connection. Therefore, we can use speech to understand our own emotions as well as those of others. With the advancement of deep learning, speech emotion recognition (SER) has gained increasing importance in fields like human-machine interaction. SER technology can analyze the emotional content of speech and provide insights into the speaker’s emotional state. This technology has the potential to improve communication and interaction between humans and machines, as well as offer valuable insights in various fields such as psychology, marketing, and customer service.This review covers a range of techniques for identifying emotions in speech and speech-text pairs. A variety of deep learning and machine learning techniques have been developed in this field, including CNN-based, LSTM-based, and SVM-based systems for processing voice signals, and BERT, GRU, and other networks for processing text. The main focus of the study is on feature extraction, classification techniques, widely used datasets, and result comparison. In other words, the review discusses how different methods can be used to extract relevant features from speech and text data, how these features can be used to classify emotions, the datasets that are commonly used for evaluating these techniques, and how the results of different methods compare to each other. Overall, this review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the current state of the field of speech emotion recognition and identify areas for further research.

articleTitle: A Review of Alzheimer’s Disease Detection from Spontaneous Speech and Text
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: In the past decade, there has been a surge in research examining the use of voice and speech analysis as a means of detecting neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s. Many studies have shown that certain acoustic features are very useful in differentiating memory changes due to normal aging from Alzheimer’s disease, and speech analysis is found to be an economical way of identifying dementia. This review aims to analyze the various algorithms used in communication-based identification and grouping of Alzheimer’s disease. A literature survey was conducted using databases such as Web of Science, Google Scholar, and Science Direct, and articles published from January 2020 to the present were included based on keywords such as “speech,” "Alzheimer’s detection," and “natural language processing.” The ADReSS, Pitt corpus, and Carolinas Conversation Collection (CCC) datasets are commonly used for the analysis of dementia from speech, and this review focuses on the various acoustic and linguistic feature engineering-based classification models drawn from 15 studies.Based on this study’s findings, it appears that a more accurate model for classifying Alzheimer’s disease can be developed by considering both linguistic and acoustic data. The review suggests that speech signals can be a useful tool for detecting dementia and can be a reliable biomarker for efficiently identifying Alzheimer’s Dementia.

articleTitle: A Survey on Image Denoising Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: The primary objective of image denoising is to suppress or discard noise or distortions from a noisy image. Images may become noisy during various processes such as image acquisition, compression, etc. Noise present in images degrades its quality; hence different techniques have been developed to successfully remove noise, without affecting image features. Therefore, image denoising is a very important task in the area of image processing. In this paper, various image denoising techniques have been explained, that have been prominent in recent times. Also, the different metrics used to evaluate these denoising models, and the loss functions that have been used in these models are also being discussed.

articleTitle: A Review on Underwater Image Enhancement Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Control, Communication and Computing (ICCC)
abstract: Underwater imaging is an innovative research area that has more benefits to researchers and scholars for mine detection, navigation, autonomous underwater imaging devices, etc. Underwater photos suffer greatly from scattering, light absorption, color cast, and the presence of artifacts, which causes the image to become increasingly blurry. At this juncture, color correction and image enhancement are highly recommended for getting a precise image with the right information. This paper summarizes the recent algorithms and their approaches in the area of underwater imaging enhancement techniques. An outline of the developing applications of underwater image processing is also presented.
